Harvest the hollow fruits when young and green at five centimetres long before the seeds turn black.
items.description: Cyclanthera pedata, known as caigua, is a herbaceous vine grown for its edible fruit, which is predominantly used as a vegetable. It is known from cultivation only, and its use goes back many centuries as evidenced by ancient phytomorphic ceramics from Peru depicting the fruits.

items.name: Bryonia cretica
items.growersTips:
Plant the tuberous roots 15cm deep in autumn in well-drained, chalky soil to mimic UK downland.
Water sparingly once established, only during prolonged summer droughts to prevent tuber rot.
Cut the climbing stems back to ground level in late autumn after the red berries have fallen.
Wear thick gloves when handling this plant to avoid skin irritation from its highly toxic sap.
Provide a sturdy trellis or plant near a deciduous hedge for the tendrils to climb naturally.
items.description: Bryonia cretica, also known as Cretan bryony or English mandrake is a perennial species of Bryonia.

items.name: Cucumis maderaspatanus
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using a heated propagator to survive chilly UK springs.
Grow this climber against a warm south-facing wall on a trellis to maximise scarce UK summer sun.
Water deeply at the base twice a week to avoid wetting leaves and preventing powdery mildew.
Pinch out the main growing tip at 1.5 metres to encourage fruiting side shoots to develop.
Plant alongside radishes to deter cucumber beetles and conserve precious greenhouse border space.
items.description: Cucumis maderaspatanus is a species of plant in the family Cucurbitaceae. The species is found throughout the tropics and subtropics, from west Africa to Australia. One of its many synonyms is Mukia maderaspatana.

items.name: Wild gherkin
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool UK spring soils.
Grow in a greenhouse or polytunnel as UK summers lack the consistent heat this desert native needs.
Water deeply at the base once a week to prevent powdery mildew on the highly sensitive wild foliage.
Train vines upward on a sturdy trellis to keep the heavy spiny melons off damp UK soil and prevent rot.
Harvest only when the green striped fruit turns fully yellow and the stem naturally begins to slip.
items.description: Cucumis africanus, the wild cucumber or wild gherkin, is a species of cucumber belonging to the genus Cucumis. It was first described by Carl Linnaeus the Younger. The species is native to Southern Africa.

items.name: Calabash
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep on their sides to prevent rotting in cold UK spring soil.
Plant out in late May after frosts, adding a handful of chicken manure pellets to each planting hole.
Train vines up a sturdy trellis to keep heavy gourds off the damp UK ground and prevent fruit rot.
Pinch out the main growing tip at 2 metres to encourage side branches where female flowers form.
Water deeply at the base, never over the leaves, to prevent powdery mildew in humid UK summers.
items.description: Lagenaria is a genus of gourd-bearing vines in the squash family (Cucurbitaceae). Lagenaria contains six species, all of which are indigenous to tropical Africa. The best-known species, the calabash or bottle gourd, L. siceraria, has been domesticated by humans, and has spread beyond Africa. The other species are not cultivated. The gourds of the various species may be harvested young and used as a vegetable. More commonly, the gourds are harvested mature, then dried, and used in making utensils. Gourds of L. siceraria have been used to store water and other liquids since ancient times. The ge

items.name: Ceratosanthes palmata
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool UK spring soils.
Grow this tender climber in a greenhouse or south-facing polytunnel to ensure crucial summer heat.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly to keep soil moist while keeping the hairy foliage dry.
Train vines up a sturdy trellis and pinch out the main growing tip at 1.5m to encourage fruiting.
Watch for powdery mildew in damp August weather and space plants 60cm apart to improve airflow.
items.description: Ceratosanthes is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Cucurbitella asperata
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using peat-free compost to counter cool UK spring soils.
Plant out in late May after frosts, spacing 90cm apart in soil enriched with well-rotted manure.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly in dry spells, keeping the hairy foliage completely dry.
Pinch out the main growing tip at five leaves to encourage lateral fruiting branches to develop.
Protect young vines from slugs using beer traps and elevate developing fruit on tiles to prevent rot.
items.description: Cucurbitella asperata is a species of flowering plant in the cucumber family, Cucurbitaceae. It is the sole species in genus Cucurbitella. It is a climbing tuberous geophyte native to southern tropical South America, ranging from Bolivia to west-central and southern Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, and northern Argentina.

items.name: Cyclanthera brachystachya
items.growersTips:
Sow indoors in April at two centimetres deep using individual pots to avoid root disturbance.
Plant out in late May after the last frost against a sturdy trellis to support the vigorous vines.
Water copiously at the base during dry summer spells to prevent the hollow exploding fruits dropping.
Train the main stem upwards then pinch out the growing tip at two metres to encourage side shoots.
Harvest the spiny pods when they reach two to three centimetres long before they burst open to seed.
items.description: Cyclanthera brachystachya, the exploding cucumber, in the cucurbit or gourd family (Cucurbitaceae), is a herbaceous vine usually grown for its curiosity value, but the fruit is also edible.

items.name: Telfairia pedata
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using a heated propagator kept at 25C to ensure germination.
Grow this tender vine inside a greenhouse or conservatory to protect it from cool UK summer nights.
Water deeply at the base twice a week during summer, keeping foliage dry to prevent powdery mildew.
Provide a sturdy trellis or overhead netting to support the heavy, vigorous climbing vines.
Prune lateral shoots back to two leaves in late summer to redirect energy into ripening the fruit.
items.description: Telfairia pedata, commonly known as oysternut, queen's nut, Zanzibar oilvine, kweme or kulekula, is a dioecious African liana which can grow up to 30 metres long, having purple-pink fringed flowers, and very large, many-seeded, drooping, ellipsoid berries which can weigh up to 15 kg. It is valuable for having edible fruit, seeds and oil.

items.name: Cucumis prophetarum
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at a depth of two centimeters using bottom heat of twenty-one Celsius.
Grow in a greenhouse or south-facing container to protect this tender perennial from UK wet winters.
Water sparingly at the base once established, allowing the gritty, free-draining soil to dry out.
Prune the main growing tip after five leaves to encourage lateral fruiting branches in midsummer.
Watch for red spider mites under glass and maintain high ventilation to prevent powdery mildew.
items.description: Cucumis prophetarum is a dioecious and prostrate or climbing perennial vine in the family Cucurbitaceae. The specific epithet (prophetarum) comes from Latin propheta, meaning "prophet".

items.name: Hedgehog cucumber
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at two centimetres deep using bottom heat of twenty-one degrees Celsius.
Grow in a greenhouse or against a south-facing wall to survive cool wet British summer nights.
Water the soil directly at the base to prevent powdery mildew on the dense bristly foliage.
Provide a sturdy trellis or mesh support to keep the heavy decorative hedgehog gourds off wet soil.
Apply a high-potassium liquid tomato feed weekly once the yellow flowers begin to appear in July.
items.description: Cucumis dipsaceus, also known as Arabian cucumber or hedgehog cucumber, is an annual climbing herb that can be found in tropical and arid locations. The plant is native to eastern Africa, first found in Sudan, southern Egypt, and Ethiopia. The developed fruits of the plant change from green to yellow and contain many seeds. The hairs that cover the oblong fruits nickname this species the “hedgehog cucumber”.

items.name: Coccinia sessilifolia
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender perennial in a heated greenhouse or sunny conservatory to survive UK cool summers.
Sow seeds in spring at a depth of two centimeters using a heated propagator set to twenty degrees.
Water deeply once a week during summer but keep the tuberous roots almost dry throughout winter.
Provide a sturdy trellis or netting for the vigorous climbing tendrils to scramble up in summer.
Overwinter the dormant tuber indoors in dry compost above five degrees to prevent rot from UK frost.
items.description: Coccinia sessilifolia is a species of Coccinia from southern Africa.

items.name: Coccinia grandiflora
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender perennial in a large pot so you can move it indoors before the first autumn frost.
Sow seeds in April at a depth of two centimetres using a heated propagator set to twenty-four Celsius.
Water deeply once a week at the base to keep soil moist but prevent waterlogging in cool UK summers.
Provide a strong trellis in a south-facing greenhouse to support the vigorous climbing tendrils.
Hand-pollinate the yellow flowers using a small paintbrush because UK insects often ignore them.
items.description: Coccinia grandiflora is an East African species of Coccinia which was first described in 1895 by Alfred Cogniaux.

items.name: Cucurbita pepo subsp. texana
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep using peat-free compost to beat the cool UK spring weather.
Plant out in late May after frosts in soil enriched with plenty of well-rotted garden compost.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly in dry summer spells to keep the shallow root system moist.
Protect young vines from slugs using beer traps or copper tape during damp British June nights.
Harvest the small striped gourds in October before the first autumn frost damages the tough skin.
items.description: Cucurbita pepo is a cultivated plant of the genus Cucurbita. It yields varieties of winter squash and pumpkin, but the most widespread varieties belong to the subspecies Cucurbita pepo subsp. pepo, called summer squash.

items.name: Kedrostis nana
items.growersTips:
Grow in a free-draining gritty loam with fifty percent pumice to prevent winter tuber rot in wet UK.
Water only when the caudex feels slightly soft, keeping it completely dry during winter dormancy.
Position in a greenhouse or south-facing windowsill to maximise summer heat and light in the UK.
Plant the tuber with the top third exposed above the soil line to prevent neck rot in damp air.
Sow seeds in April at twenty-one degrees Celsius using a heated propagator to ensure germination.
items.description: Kedrostis is a genus of ± 35 species climbing or trailing herbs in the family Cucurbitaceae. Its native range is tropical Africa and Asia.

items.name: Coastal manroot
items.growersTips:
Plant the massive tuber fifteen centimetres deep in sharply draining grit to prevent winter rot.
Water deeply once a week in spring then stop watering entirely when the vine dies back in summer.
Sow seeds in deep pots during autumn and leave outdoors for winter chill to break dormancy.
Provide a sturdy trellis or fence by April to support the rapid five-metre scramble of vines.
Protect emerging spring shoots from slugs using beer traps as the wet UK climate encourages pests.
items.description: Marah oregana, the Oregon manroot, coastal manroot or western wild-cucumber, is a common manroot of the northwest coast of the United States. It ranges from California north to Vancouver Island in southwestern Canada.

items.name: Echinocystis lobata
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at two centimetres deep in peat-free compost to protect from late frosts.
Soak the hard-coated seeds in warm water for twenty-four hours before sowing to speed germination.
Provide a sturdy trellis or netting by May to support the rapid five-metre climbing habit of vines.
Water the base deeply twice a week during dry UK summer spells to prevent powdery mildew on leaves.
Watch for slugs and snails on young spring shoots and protect them with organic wool pellets.
items.description: Echinocystis is a monotypic genus in the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae. The sole species is E. lobata, commonly called wild cucumber and prickly cucumber. It is an annual, sprawling plant that is native to North America. Sicyos angulatus, common name "bur cucumber", is an annual plant with a similar clinging vine growth but different-appearing flowers and seed pods.

items.name: Cucumeropsis mannii
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to survive the cool UK spring.
Grow inside a greenhouse or polytunnel to provide the high humidity and 20C plus heat this vine needs.
Water the soil deeply twice a week at the base to keep leaves dry and prevent powdery mildew.
Train the vigorous vines up a sturdy trellis to keep the heavy white-seeded gourds off damp soil.
Hand pollinate the yellow male and female flowers in midsummer using a soft brush to ensure fruit set.
items.description: Melothria sphaerocarpa is a species of melon native from southern Mexico and the Dominican Republic through Central America to tropical South America. It has been introduced to western tropical Africa, where has been known under the synonym Cucumeropsis mannii, and is grown for food and as a source of oil, more often for the seed oil than for the fruit.

items.name: Herpetospermum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool UK spring soils.
Plant out in June against a south-facing wall to maximise sun exposure and shelter from cold winds.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly to keep soil moist without wetting leaves to prevent mildew.
Train the vigorous vines up a sturdy trellis or A-frame to keep the heavy fruits off damp UK soil.
Prune the main growing tip when it reaches two metres to encourage fruiting lateral branches.
items.description: Herpetospermum is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Dactyliandra
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at a depth of 2cm using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool UK spring soils
Grow in a greenhouse or south-facing polytunnel to provide the high heat and humidity this vine needs
Water deeply at the base twice a week keeping foliage dry to prevent powdery mildew in damp UK summers
Train the climbing tendrils onto a sturdy trellis or netting weekly to support heavy fruiting stems
Prune the main growing tip when it reaches two metres to encourage productive lateral fruiting side shoots
items.description: Dactyliandra is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Ampelosicyos
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using a heated propagator to mimic tropical warmth.
Grow this vigorous climber inside a polytunnel or greenhouse to survive cool UK summer nights.
Water heavily at the base twice a week during summer, keeping the foliage dry to prevent mildew.
Train the heavy vines onto sturdy trellis wires spaced 30cm apart to support the weight of fruit.
Incorporate well-rotted manure into the soil in autumn to provide the rich nutrients required.
items.description: Ampelosicyos is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Coccinia abyssinica
items.growersTips:
Plant the tuberous root ten centimetres deep in late spring once all risk of spring frost has passed
Grow in a container filled with gritty loam to easily move the plant indoors before winter frosts
Water deeply once a week during summer but keep the soil completely dry during winter dormancy
Provide a sturdy trellis in a south-facing greenhouse to support the vigorous climbing annual stems
Watch for red spider mites in dry glasshouse conditions and mist the foliage to increase humidity
items.description: Coccinia abyssinica is an Ethiopian species of Coccinia which was first described by Jean-Baptiste Lamarck. The tuber is under its Oromo name anchote a well-known local crop, but also the leaves are eaten.

items.name: Telfairia
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 3cm depth using bottom heat of 25C to overcome the cool UK spring.
Grow in a greenhouse or south-facing polytunnel to meet the high heat demand of this African vine.
Provide a sturdy trellis at least two meters high to support the heavy, vigorous climbing tendrils.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly to keep soil moist but never waterlogged in damp UK summers.
Prune the main shoot at one meter to encourage lateral branching and increase leaf yield.
items.description: Telfairia is a small genus of flowering plants in the squash family which are native to Africa. They include Telfairia occidentalis, the fluted pumpkin, which is an important vegetable in Nigeria and other African nations. It is also known as the oyster nut, a common name it shares with its relative Telfairia pedata. These are woody and herbaceous dioecious vines which bear squashlike fruits that contain large, nutritious oily seeds. The third species is Telfairia batesii which is very rare and not cultivated.

items.name: Cayaponia
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to survive the cool UK spring.
Grow in a greenhouse or against a south-facing wall in fertile soil with a pH between 6.0 and 6.8.
Water deeply at the base twice a week to keep soil moist but avoid wetting leaves to prevent rot.
Provide a strong trellis or netting by June to support its vigorous climbing vines and heavy fruit.
Check weekly for powdery mildew in August and space plants 90cm apart to improve air circulation.
items.description: Cayaponia is among the largest genera in the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae, with 74 species. The plants are referred to as melonleaf. They are common from the southern United States to South America. Some species are also found in western Africa, Madagascar, and Fernando de Noronha, which is about 354 km (220 mi) off the coast of Brazil.

items.name: Cyclanthera carthagenensis
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 20C to counter chilly UK springs.
Plant out in late May against a south-facing wall to maximise sun exposure and shelter from wind.
Water deeply at the base twice a week during dry spells to prevent powdery mildew on the foliage.
Provide a sturdy 2-metre trellis or netting by June to support the vigorous climbing tendrils.
Harvest the small green fruits when they reach 3-5cm long before they become tough and seedy.
items.description: Cyclanthera carthagenensis is a species of flowering plants in the family Cucurbitaceae native to Mexico to tropical South America. It is introduced and considered invasive in Cuba. It is often known by the synonym Rytidostylis carthagenensis.

items.name: Cucumis argenteus
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool British springs.
Plant out in late May in a sunny, sheltered spot using raised mounds to improve cold soil drainage.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly to keep soil damp but avoid wetting leaves to prevent mildew.
Pinch out the main growing tip at five leaves to encourage lateral fruiting branches to develop.
Grow alongside radishes to deter cucumber beetles and under fleece until flowers need pollination.
items.description: Cucumis argenteus commonly known as snake vine, is a flowering vine in the family Cucurbitaceae. It has yellow flowers, red berries, variable leaves and grows in Western Australia, Queensland, South Australia and the Northern Territory.

items.name: Citrullus
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at two centimetres deep in individual pots using a heated propagator.
Grow plants in a greenhouse or polytunnel to ensure they get the high heat and humidity they need.
Water deeply at the base twice a week to keep soil moist but keep the foliage dry to avoid rot.
Place a slate or tile under developing fruit to protect it from damp soil and prevent rotting.
Hand pollinate female flowers using a small brush with pollen from male flowers on a sunny morning.
items.description: Citrullus is a genus of seven species of desert vines, among which Citrullus lanatus is an important crop.

items.name: Marah fabacea
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds individually in deep pots in autumn to allow the large taproot to develop over winter.
Plant out in spring in a sheltered south-facing spot with gritty soil to prevent winter root rot.
Provide a sturdy trellis or fence by May to support the vigorous climbing tendrils as they grow.
Water deeply at the base once a week during dry summer spells, keeping the foliage entirely dry.
Protect emerging spring shoots from slugs and snails using organic bait or copper tape barriers.
items.description: Marah fabacea, the California manroot or bigroot, is the most common of the manroot species native to California. Its range throughout the state subsumes nearly the entire ranges of all the other California native manroots species and intergrades. Hybrids between California manroot and other species of Marah are common.

items.name: Marah macrocarpa
items.growersTips:
Plant the massive tuber at least twenty centimetres deep in gritty soil to protect it from UK frosts.
Provide a sturdy trellis or south-facing wall to support its rapid three-metre spring vine growth.
Water deeply only during active spring growth, then keep the soil bone-dry during summer dormancy.
Protect emerging spring shoots from slugs and snails using organic grit barriers or beer traps.
Sow seeds in autumn in deep pots to accommodate the long taproot before planting out in spring.
items.description: Marah macrocarpa is a species of plant in the genus Marah commonly referred to as chilicothe, wild cucumber, manroot or bigroot. It is a perennial herb with a large tuber native to Southern California and northern Baja California. It grows in a diverse number of habitats in coastal and inland regions. A member of the gourd family, it produces a large, green, prickly fruit. Indigenous peoples traditionally used it for treating hair loss and pain relief. All parts of the plant are toxic, as it contains cucurbitacins and ribosome-inactivating proteins.

items.name: Ctenolepis garcinii
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using a heated propagator to survive chilly UK springs.
Grow this tender climber inside a greenhouse or polytunnel to ensure the high heat it requires.
Water deeply at the base twice a week keeping foliage dry to prevent powdery mildew in damp UK air.
Train the climbing vines onto a sturdy trellis or netting to keep the heavy fruits off wet soil.
Apply a high-potassium tomato fertiliser weekly once yellow flowers appear to boost fruit set.
items.description: Blastania garcinii, also known as Garcin's bur cucumber, is a tender climber of the family Cucurbitaceae. It is one of the three species of the genus Blastania. The species was named after French botanist Laurent Garcin, who traveled India in the 18th century.

items.name: Gerrardanthus lobatus
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender caudiciform in a gritty, free-draining loam-based compost to prevent root rot.
Position the swollen caudex entirely above the soil line when potting to protect it from damp.
Water only when the soil dries out completely from spring to autumn, keeping it dry in winter.
Overwinter indoors on a sunny windowsill or heated greenhouse keeping temperatures above ten Celsius.
Provide a trellis or thin stakes in spring for the vigorous annual climbing stems to scramble up.
items.description: Gerrardanthus lobatus is a species of plant native to eastern and southern Africa. It is a popular pot plant that grows in deciduous bushland, woodland, wooded grassland in rocky places, and also in hygrophilous and riverine forests and clearings.

items.name: Gerrardanthus macrorhizus
items.growersTips:
Grow this caudiciform in a gritty, free-draining loam-based compost with the tuber sitting on top.
Keep completely dry from October to April in a frost-free greenhouse or windowsill above 10C.
Water only when the soil dries out fully during summer, avoiding wetting the exposed swollen base.
Provide a trellis or stakes in May for the vigorous annual climbing vines to cling to as they grow.
Check the underside of leaves weekly in summer for red spider mites, which thrive in dry indoor air.
items.description: Gerrardanthus macrorhizus, also known as bigfoot, is a species of plant native to southern Africa. It is a popular pot plant.

items.name: Gynostemma
items.growersTips:
Grow in a container with a trellis so you can move it into a frost-free greenhouse for UK winters.
Plant in moisture-retentive, humus-rich soil, keeping the crown exactly level with the soil surface.
Water consistently to keep soil damp but never waterlogged, especially during dry UK summer spells.
Prune vines back to 15cm in early spring to stimulate vigorous new leafy growth for tea harvesting.
Protect young spring shoots from slugs and snails using beer traps or physical barriers in damp UKs.
items.description: Gynostemma is a genus of perennial climbing vines in the cucumber, gourd, and melon family, comprising at least 19 species, all native to the tropical East or Far East, inclusive of the Himalayas: China ; the islands of Japan; Malaysia; and New Guinea. The term Gynostemma is derived from Ancient Greek γυνή meaning "woman" or "female", and στέμμα meaning "wreath" or "garland". In (post-)classical Latin the form stemma is attested as Greek loanword. In Ancient Greek and Latin, stemma is of neuter gender. German-Dutch botanist Carl Ludwig Blume described Gynostemma from two species he named: G. p

items.name: Alsomitra
items.growersTips:
Grow Alsomitra in a heated greenhouse or conservatory keeping winter temperatures above fifteen Celsius
Sow seeds in spring on their edge five millimetres deep in free-draining peat-free compost with grit
Train the climbing vines up a sturdy trellis or overhead wires to support the heavy summer growth
Water thoroughly once the top centimetre of soil dries out then reduce watering during winter dormancy
Watch for glasshouse red spider mite under leaves and apply biological controls like Phytoseiulus
items.description: Alsomitra is a genus of the plant family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Cucurbita
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep on their sides to prevent rotting before outdoor planting.
Plant out in late May into soil enriched with a bucket of well-rotted manure per plant to feed them.
Water deeply at the base, not over leaves, to prevent powdery mildew in humid UK summer weather.
Sink a plastic pot next to the main stem to channel water directly to the deep roots when watering.
Place a tile or slate under developing fruits in August to stop them rotting on damp British soil.
items.description: Cucurbita is a genus of herbaceous fruits in the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae, native to the Andes and Mesoamerica. Five edible species are grown and consumed for their flesh and seeds. They are variously known as squash, pumpkin, or gourd, depending on species, variety, and local parlance. Other kinds of gourd, also called bottle-gourds, are native to Africa and belong to the genus Lagenaria, which is in the same family and subfamily as Cucurbita, but in a different tribe; their young fruits are eaten much like those of the Cucurbita species.

items.name: Zehneria scabra
items.growersTips:
Plant tubers 10cm deep in late April using grit-enriched loam to prevent winter rot in wet UK soils.
Water deeply once a week at the base during dry summer spells to prevent powdery mildew on foliage.
Provide a sturdy trellis or obelisk by May to support the vigorous climbing tendrils as they grow.
Cut back dead vines to ground level in late autumn and mulch heavily with bark to protect from frost.
Grow in a south-facing sheltered spot or cold frame to ensure enough summer heat for fruit set.
items.description: Zehneria scabra is a perennial climbing or trailing herb that belong to the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Acanthosicyos
items.growersTips:
Grow Acanthosicyos horridus in a heated greenhouse with sandy, free-draining cactus compost.
Water only when the soil is completely dry, mimicking desert conditions to prevent root rot.
Sow seeds individually in deep pots at a depth of two centimeters to protect the long taproot.
Install a sturdy trellis early to support the heavy, sprawling, extremely thorny green stems.
Maintain a minimum winter temperature of twelve degrees Celsius to keep this desert melon alive.
items.description: Acanthosicyos is a genus of thorny shrubs of the botanical family Cucurbitaceae, subfamily Cucurbitoideae. The genus name comes from Ancient Greek ἄκανθα (ákantha), meaning "thorn", and σικύος (sikúos), meaning "gourd".

items.name: Benincasa
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2.5cm deep using bottom heat of 21C to survive the cool UK spring.
Grow in a greenhouse or against a south-facing wall in fertile soil with a pH of 6.0 to 6.8.
Hand-pollinate the yellow flowers midday using a cotton swab because UK pollinator activity is low.
Train the heavy vines up a sturdy trellis and support swelling winter melons with net hammocks.
Water deeply at the base to keep soil moist but avoid wetting leaves to prevent powdery mildew.
items.description:
Benincasa is a genus of flowering plants in the cucumber family, Cucurbitaceae. It includes two species native to Indomalaya and Australasia:Benincasa fistulosa (Stocks) H.Schaef. & S.S.Renner – tinda
Benincasa hispida (Thunb.) Cogn. – wax gourd

items.name: Echinopepon racemosus
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 20C to combat cool UK spring soil.
Plant out in late May against a south-facing wall to maximise sun exposure and shelter from wind.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly in summer, keeping foliage dry to prevent powdery mildew.
Provide a sturdy trellis or netting at planting time to support its rapid, curling tendrils.
Apply a high-potassium liquid tomato feed fortnightly once the first white flowers appear.
items.description: Echinopepon racemosus is a species of flowering plant in the genus Echinopepon, native to Latin America. A vine, its densely echinate fruits are dehiscent, but not explosive.

items.name: Cayaponia tayuya
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at twenty-one degrees Celsius using deep pots to protect taproots.
Grow this tender vine inside a greenhouse or polytunnel to ensure the high heat and humidity needed.
Provide a strong trellis or netting by May to support the vigorous climbing tendrils as they grow.
Water deeply at the base twice a week to keep soil moist but prevent waterlogging and root rot.
Apply a high-potassium liquid tomato feed every two weeks once the vine reaches two meters tall.
items.description: Cayaponia tayuya is a vine that grows in the Amazon region of South America, in the nations of Brazil, Bolivia and Peru. Its roots are used in herbal medicine.

items.name: Seyrigia
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Madagascan succulent in a heated greenhouse or indoors to survive UK winter cold.
Water only when the gritty cactus compost dries out completely, keeping it bone dry through winter.
Propagate by taking stem cuttings in late spring and letting them callus over before potting up.
Position in a south-facing window or bright conservatory to provide maximum possible UK sunlight.
Check regularly for mealybugs nestled in the jointed stems and treat immediately with organic oil.
items.description:
Seyrigia may refer to:Seyrigia (beetle), a genus of insects in the family Buprestidae
Seyrigia (plant), a genus of plants in the family Cucurbitaceae

items.name: Melothria
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at two centimetres deep using bottom heat of twenty-one degrees Celsius.
Plant out in late May only after the last frost, spacing vines forty centimetres apart in full sun.
Provide a sturdy trellis or netting immediately at planting to support their rapid climbing habit.
Water consistently at the base to keep soil moist but not soggy, avoiding wet foliage to prevent rot.
Harvest when fruits are the size of grapes and drop naturally, before they turn yellow and bitter.
items.description: Melothria is a genus of flowering plants in the family Cucurbitaceae, native to the Americas from the United States to Argentina, and with some introductions in Africa and elsewhere. A number of Old World species formerly in Melothria were reassigned to Cucumis.

items.name: Trochomeria
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender African caudiciform in a greenhouse or sunny windowsill to protect from UK frost.
Plant seeds 1cm deep in a free-draining mix of equal parts John Innes number two and horticultural grit.
Water deeply only when the soil is dry, then keep completely dry in winter to prevent tuber rot.
Watch for red spider mite under glass and treat early with biological controls like Phytoseiulus.
Train the climbing annual vines up a small trellis or moss pole during the active summer growth.
items.description: Trochomeria is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Abobra tenuifolia
items.growersTips:
Plant tuberous roots 10cm deep in late spring after frosts in free-draining sandy loam facing south.
Provide a sturdy trellis or wires for the vigorous climbing tendrils to scale during summer.
Water deeply once a week at the base during dry summer spells to support the fleshy red fruits.
Lift the tender tubers in November and store them in dry peat-free compost in a frost-free shed.
Grow male and female plants close together to ensure pollination and successful red berry crop.
items.description: Abobra is a monotypic genus of the gourd family containing the one species Abobra tenuifolia. It is a diecious, perennial climbing plant reaching up to the height of 4 m (13 ft). It is native to South America and is sometimes cultivated as ornamental plants and also for its edible fruits. The flowers exude a strong fragrance and are of pale green color and blossom between July and August. The seeds ripen between September and October. The fruit is ovoid and has a diameter of 14 mm. Common names include cranberry gourd.

items.name: Cucumis anguria
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool UK spring soils.
Grow in a greenhouse or against a south-facing wall to maximise heat for pollination by mid-July.
Water deeply at the base twice a week to prevent powdery mildew on the dense, trailing foliage.
Train vines up a sturdy trellis to keep the heavy, spiny gherkins off damp, slug-prone UK soil.
Harvest the gherkins weekly when they reach 4cm long and are still firm, pale green, and tender.
items.description: Cucumis anguria, commonly known as maroon cucumber, West Indian gherkin, maxixe, burr gherkin, cackrey, and West Indian gourd, is a vine that is indigenous to Africa, but has become naturalized in the New World, and is cultivated in many places. It is similar and related to the common cucumber (C. sativus) and its cultivars are known as gherkins.

items.name: Cogniauxia
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 20C in deep pots to protect taproots before late May transplanting.
Grow against a south-facing wall on a sturdy trellis to maximise limited UK summer sun and warmth.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly to keep soil moist but prevent powdery mildew on the foliage.
Prune the main stem at two metres to encourage lateral fruiting branches and speed up UK ripening.
Feed weekly with high-potassium tomato fertiliser once female flowers appear to boost fruit set.
items.description: Cogniauxia is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Cucurbita pepo
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep in 9cm pots, keeping them at 20C before planting out in June.
Dig a 30cm deep hole in May, fill with rotted manure, and plant your pumpkin on top of this mound.
Water deeply at the base twice a week in dry spells, keeping the leaves dry to prevent powdery mildew.
Elevate developing fruits onto bricks or wooden boards in August to prevent rot from damp UK soil.
Cut the vine tips in late August to redirect all plant energy into ripening the existing pumpkins.
items.description: Cucurbita pepo is a cultivated plant of the genus Cucurbita. It yields varieties of winter squash and pumpkin, but the most widespread varieties belong to the subspecies Cucurbita pepo subsp. pepo, called summer squash.

items.name: Gurania
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep using a heated propagator to survive the cool UK spring.
Grow this vigorous climber up a sturdy trellis in a south-facing greenhouse to maximise UK sun.
Water the soil deeply twice a week keeping foliage dry to prevent powdery mildew in damp UK air.
Prune lateral shoots to two leaves once fruit sets to focus energy in short British summers.
Feed weekly with high-potassium liquid tomato fertiliser once the first exotic orange flowers open.
items.description: Gurania is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Solena
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool UK spring soils
Grow Solena against a south-facing wall or in a polytunnel to maximize crucial summer heat units
Water deeply at the base twice weekly keeping foliage dry to prevent powdery mildew in damp UK air
Train the climbing vines up a sturdy trellis to keep the heavy gourds off wet ground and stop rot
Prune the main stem after five leaves to encourage lateral fruiting branches for a bigger harvest
items.description:
Solena may refer to:Solena (bivalve), a genus of bivalves in the family Solenidae
Solena (plant), a genus of plants in the family Cucurbitaceae
Solena, a genus of plants in the family Rubiaceae, synonym of Posoqueria

items.name: Bryonia alba
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in autumn in cold frames to allow winter chilling to break dormancy before spring warmth.
Grow in well-drained, alkaline chalky soil, mimicking its native UK hedgerow and scrub habitats.
Provide a sturdy trellis or allow it to scramble naturally over deciduous shrubs in early spring.
Water deeply once a week during dry summer spells, keeping the large tuberous root system moist.
Wear thick gloves when pruning back the vigorous vines in late autumn to avoid skin irritation.
items.description: Bryonia alba is a vigorous vine in the family Cucurbitaceae, found in Europe and Northern Iran. It has a growth habit similar to kudzu, which gives it a highly destructive potential outside its native range as a noxious weed. Other common names include false mandrake, English mandrake, wild vine, and wild hops, wild nep, tamus, ladies' seal, and tetterbury.

items.name: Zehneria
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at two centimetres deep using bottom heat of twenty-one degrees Celsius.
Grow in a greenhouse or sunny south-facing patio container to survive cool UK summer temperatures.
Water consistently at the base to keep soil damp but never waterlogged to prevent root rot issues.
Train the vigorous climbing vines up a sturdy trellis or netting to keep the tiny fruits clean.
Watch closely for powdery mildew in late August and improve air circulation around the foliage.
items.description: Zehneria is a genus of flowering plants – of vines in the cucumber and gourd family, Cucurbitaceae. It contains about 35 species ranging from Africa, through Southeast Asia to Australia and Oceania. The name honours botanical artist Joseph Zehner.

items.name: Acanthosicyos horridus
items.growersTips:
Grow this desert native in a heated greenhouse or conservatory to survive the cold UK climate.
Use a gritty cactus compost mix to ensure the rapid drainage this taprooted melon absolutely needs.
Water deeply only when the soil is bone dry, then withhold water entirely during winter dormancy.
Position in the brightest south-facing spot possible to mimic the intense Namibian desert sun.
Wear thick leather gloves when handling to protect your hands from the extremely sharp, leafless spines.
items.description: Acanthosicyos horridus is an unusual melon that is endemic to the Namib desert. In English it is known as Nara, butter-nuts, or butterpips; in one of the Khoisan languages it is locally called ǃnaras or ǃnara.

items.name: Psiguria
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender tropical vine in a heated greenhouse or conservatory to survive cool UK summers.
Sow seeds 2cm deep in individual pots of peat-free compost on a heated propagator mat at 21C in April.
Water the soil deeply only when the top 3cm dries out to prevent root rot in damp UK conditions.
Train the vigorous climbing stems onto a sturdy trellis or wire support system to save glasshouse space.
Watch closely for glasshouse whitefly and red spider mite, treating immediately with biological controls.
items.description: Psiguria is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Zanonia
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using a heated propagator kept at a constant 21C.
Grow in a greenhouse or south-facing conservatory to meet the high heat needs of this exotic vine.
Water the base weekly with tepid rainwater to keep soil moist but prevent stem rot at the collar.
Provide a sturdy trellis or netting for the climbing tendrils to support the heavy winged fruits.
Feed fortnightly with a high-potassium liquid tomato fertilizer once the first flowers appear.
items.description: Zanonia is a monotypic genus in the flowering plant family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Apodanthera undulata
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool UK spring soils.
Grow in a greenhouse or south-facing polytunnel to provide the high summer heat this species needs.
Water deeply at the base weekly once fruit sets, keeping foliage dry to prevent powdery mildew.
Incorporate well-rotted manure into sandy, free-draining soil to mimic its native arid riverbeds.
Train the vigorous vines onto a sturdy trellis to keep the heavy gourds off damp UK ground.
items.description: Apodanthera undulata, common name melon loco, is a plant species native to the south-western United States and in Mexico as far south as Oaxaca.

items.name: Coccinia intermedia
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool UK spring soils.
Grow this tender perennial vine inside a greenhouse or polytunnel to ensure crucial summer warmth.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly once fruit sets, keeping foliage dry to prevent powdery mildew.
Provide a sturdy trellis or netting by June to support the vigorous climbing tendrils of this vine.
Hand-pollinate the yellow flowers using a small brush to guarantee fruit set in insect-poor glasshouses.
items.description: Coccinia intermedia is a species of Coccinia which was first described in 2011 by Norbert Holstein.

items.name: Zehneria maysorensis
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender climber in pots of peat-free loam compost to easily move indoors before autumn frost.
Sow seeds in April at 1cm depth using a heated propagator kept at a constant 20C to ensure germination.
Water deeply at the base twice a week in summer, keeping the foliage dry to prevent powdery mildew.
Provide a sturdy trellis or pea netting in May for the vigorous climbing tendrils to scramble up.
Overwinter dormant tubers in dry compost inside a frost-free greenhouse or shed kept above 5C.
items.description: Zehneria maysorensis  is a perennial climbing or trailing herb that belongs to the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Xerosicyos
items.growersTips:
Grow in a gritty free-draining cactus compost and keep above ten degrees Celsius in winter indoors.
Water only when the soil is bone dry then soak fully, stopping water completely from November to March.
Place on a south-facing windowsill to maximise light and prevent the round succulent leaves dropping.
Prune leggy stems in late spring using sterile shears to encourage a bushier climbing habit.
Check leaf joins weekly for mealybugs, treating infestations immediately with an alcohol-soaked swab.
items.description: Xerosicyos is a flowering plant genus of the family Cucurbitaceae. Its name comes from Greek xeros and sicyos ("cucumber"). There are six species, all endemic to Madagascar.

items.name: Eureiandra balfourii
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender caudiciform climber in a heated greenhouse or conservatory to survive UK winters.
Sow seeds in spring at a depth of 1cm in a free-draining sandy loam mix with extra perlite.
Water sparingly from spring to autumn, allowing the soil to dry out completely between waterings.
Provide a sturdy trellis or vertical wires for the climbing annual vines to cling to as they grow.
Keep the tuberous caudex completely dry and dormant in a frost-free greenhouse throughout winter.
items.description: Eureiandra balfourii is a species of plant in the family Cucurbitaceae. It is endemic to Socotra in Yemen. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry forests.

items.name: Marah horridus
items.growersTips:
Plant tubers 15cm deep in autumn using gritty, free-draining soil to prevent winter rot in wet UK clay.
Water deeply once a week during spring growth, then stop watering entirely when summer dormancy begins.
Provide a sturdy trellis or fence by April to support the rapid, heavy climbing vines of this plant.
Protect emerging spring shoots from slugs and snails using organic grit barriers or beer traps.
Grow in a south-facing, sheltered spot to maximise summer heat and mimic its native dry habitat.
items.description: Marah horrida, common name Sierra manroot, is a species of flowering plant in the family Cucurbitaceae, endemic to the foothills of the Sierra Nevada and the Tehachapi Mountains in California. It grows in open and shrubby areas below 1,000 m (3,300 ft) elevation.

items.name: Schizocarpum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep using bottom heat of 21C to survive the cool UK spring.
Grow in a greenhouse or against a south-facing wall in fertile soil with a pH between 6.0 and 6.8.
Water deeply at the base twice a week to keep soil damp but prevent waterlogging and powdery mildew.
Provide a sturdy trellis or netting for the climbing tendrils to support the heavy, hollow fruits.
Hand-pollinate the yellow flowers using a small paintbrush if UK pollinator activity is low in June.
items.description: Schizocarpum is a genus of nine accepted species of flowering plants of the family Cucurbitaceae. It is native to Mexico and Central America.

items.name: Bryonia dioica
items.growersTips:
Plant the large tuberous roots 10cm deep in autumn using well-drained, chalky or alkaline soil.
Grow this vigorous climber against a sturdy south-facing trellis to support its heavy summer growth.
Water newly planted tubers weekly in spring, then rely on natural UK rainfall once established.
Prune the entire vine down to ground level in late autumn after the red berries have fully withered.
Wear thick gloves when handling to avoid skin irritation from the highly toxic sap and red berries.
items.description: Bryonia dioica, known by the common names red bryony and white bryony, also English mandrake or ladies' seal, is a perennial climbing vine indigenous to Central and Southern Europe. It is a flowering plant in the cucumber family Cucurbitaceae with five-pointed leaves and blue or white flowers. The vine produces a red berry fruit.

items.name: Coccinia grandis
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender perennial in a large pot so you can move it into a heated greenhouse for UK winters.
Sow seeds 2cm deep in a heated propagator at 25C in April to combat the cool British spring weather.
Water deeply twice a week to keep soil moist but never waterlogged to prevent root rot in UK clay.
Hand-pollinate the yellow-white flowers daily in summer as UK native bees often ignore this vine.
Prune back the vigorous vines to 30cm in late autumn before moving the pot indoors for dormancy.
items.description: Coccinia grandis, the ivy gourd, also known as scarlet gourd, or Tindora, is a tropical vine. It grows primarily in tropical climates and is commonly found in the Indian states where it forms a part of the local cuisine. Coccinia grandis is cooked as a vegetable dish.

items.name: Cayaponia espelina
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Brazilian climber in a heated greenhouse or conservatory to survive UK winters.
Sow seeds in April at 2cm depth in 9cm pots of free-draining peat-free compost on a heated mat.
Water deeply once a week at the base to keep soil moist but avoid waterlogging the tuberous roots.
Train the vigorous vines up a sturdy trellis or netting system to keep the heavy foliage off the ground.
Apply a high-potassium liquid tomato feed every two weeks once the yellow flowers begin to appear.
items.description: Cayaponia espelina, also known as the São Caetano melon, is a plant native to Brazil. It is a diuretic and aids in the treatment of diarrhea and syphilis. The fruits are occasionally eaten by the maned wolf.

items.name: Polyclathra
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at two centimetres deep using bottom heat of twenty-one degrees Celsius.
Plant out in late May after frosts in rich soil mixed with plenty of well-rotted garden compost.
Grow up a sturdy trellis or A-frame to keep the heavy climbing vines and fruits off damp UK soil.
Water deeply at the base twice a week to prevent blossom end rot while keeping the foliage dry.
Hand-pollinate the yellow flowers with a paintbrush if cool UK summers limit active bee visits.
items.description: Polyclathra is a genus of the gourd family. It has the synonyms Pentaclathra, Pittiera, and Roseanthus. Its corolla is white.

items.name: Diplocyclos
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to counter chilly UK spring soils.
Grow this vigorous climber up a sturdy trellis in a south-facing, sheltered suntrap or greenhouse.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly in dry summer spells, keeping the foliage dry to avoid rot.
Prune the main vine at two meters to encourage side shoots and increase the yield of striped fruit.
Watch for red spider mites under leaves in dry glasshouses and spray with water to raise humidity.
items.description: Diplocyclos is a genus of climbing or trailing vine in the family Cucurbitaceae. The genus comprises four or five species. D. palmatus is pantropical in distribution and the remainder of species are restricted to Africa. All species are found within rainforest and the moister woodland types.

items.name: Ivy Gourd
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to survive the cool UK spring.
Grow ivy gourd in a greenhouse or south-facing conservatory to meet its high heat requirement.
Water deeply twice a week at the base to keep soil moist but prevent powdery mildew on leaves.
Provide a sturdy trellis or netting for this vigorous climber to keep the heavy fruits off the wet soil.
Apply a high-potassium liquid tomato feed every two weeks once the yellow flowers begin to appear.
items.description: The scarlet gourds are a genus with 25 species. It is distributed in sub-Saharan Africa and with one species, C. grandis also in South Asia and Southeast Asia, and it is also introduced into the New World. Incidentally, C. grandis is also a cultivated crop and it is used for culinary and medical purposes.

items.name: Schizopepon dioicus
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at two centimeters deep using bottom heat to survive cool UK springs.
Grow up a sturdy trellis in a south-facing sheltered spot to protect weak vines from UK winds.
Water deeply at the base twice a week during dry summer spells to prevent powdery mildew on leaves.
Prune the main growing tip at one meter high to encourage lateral fruiting branches to develop.
Harvest the small spiky gourds in September before the first autumn frosts rot the delicate vines.
items.description: Schizopepon is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Cucurbita digitata
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to survive short UK summers.
Grow in a raised bed of sandy loam with added grit to prevent root rot in wet UK autumn weather.
Water deeply only at the base once a week to avoid powdery mildew on the highly lobed leaves.
Train the vigorous five-finger vines onto a sturdy south-facing trellis to maximise UK sunshine.
Hand-pollinate the yellow flowers in morning hours as UK native bees often ignore this wild species.
items.description: Cucurbita digitata is a species of flowering plant in the squash family known by the common names fingerleaf gourd and bitter squash. It is similar to Cucurbita californica, Cucurbita cordata, Cucurbita cylindrata, and Cucurbita palmata and all these species hybridize readily. These species form the only restricted xerophyte species group in the genus Cucurbita. Each member of this species group is native to the Southwestern United States and Northwestern Mexico where they are relatively uncommon. Each group member is found in hot, arid regions with low rainfall. They prefer soil that is loose

items.name: Cucurbita okeechobeensis
items.growersTips:
Sow indoors in April at 2cm deep in 9cm pots using a heated propagator to beat the cool UK spring.
Plant out in June after the last frost into soil enriched with a full wheelbarrow of rotted manure.
Water deeply at the base twice a week in dry summer spells, keeping the hairy leaves entirely dry.
Train the vigorous vines along a sturdy trellis to keep the heavy fruits off damp, slug-prone soil.
Pinch out the growing tips in August to force the plant to ripen its existing fruits before frost.
items.description:
Cucurbita okeechobeensis, the Okeechobee gourd, is a species of gourd belonging to the family Cucurbitaceae, native to Mexico and the United States. There are two subspecies; one is endemic to Florida, primarily in the region around Lake Okeechobee, the other to the State of Veracruz in eastern Mexico. Once abundant, it has state and federal listing as an endangered species.
One of its peculiarities is the yellow corolla not so common in other Cucurbita species.

items.name: Brandegea bigelovii
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender desert native in a terracotta pot of 50 percent grit to survive wet UK winters.
Water only when the gritty soil is bone dry, stopping completely from October to April to stop rot.
Sow seeds in April at a depth of one centimetre using a heated propagator set to 21 degrees Celsius.
Provide a sturdy trellis or wire frame in a south-facing greenhouse to support the climbing vines.
Watch closely for glasshouse red spider mite during hot dry spells in midsummer and mist foliage.
items.description: Brandegea is a monotypic genus containing the single species Brandegea bigelovii, the desert starvine. This sprawling perennial vine in the squash family is native to the deserts of California, Arizona, and northern Mexico. The distinctive small, dark-green leaves are variable in shape but are usually a deeply lobed long-fingered palmate shape. They are heavily speckled with white oil glands. The vine bears tendrils, tiny five-pointed white flowers only 2 or 3 millimeters wide, and small, dry, prickly fruits 5 or 6 millimeters in length and holding a single seed. The plant grows from a deep ta

items.name: Marah macrocarpa
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds five centimetres deep in autumn to allow winter cold to naturally break their dormancy.
Grow in deep terracotta pots to accommodate the massive tuber and protect it from winter wet rot.
Provide a sturdy trellis in full sun by April to support the rapid spring climb of the vines.
Water deeply once a week during spring growth but keep the soil completely dry during summer dormancy.
Protect emerging spring shoots from slugs using beer traps or copper tape as they are highly vulnerable.
items.description:
Marah may refer to:Marah (plant) or manroot, a kind of wild cucumber
Marah (band), an American rock band
Marah (Bible), one of the locations which the Torah identifies as having been travelled through by the Israelites during the Exodus
Micha Marah, Belgian popular singer
Marah, a variant of the Irish name O'Meara
Marah, (Arabic) Joy or happiness
Marah Wagner, American ice hockey player

items.name: Apodanthera undulata
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool UK spring soils.
Grow in a greenhouse or against a south-facing brick wall to maximize essential summer heat units.
Water deeply at the base twice a week to keep soil moist but prevent powdery mildew on the foliage.
Train the vigorous vines onto a sturdy trellis to keep the heavy gourds off damp UK ground soil.
Incorporate well-rotted manure into the planting site to meet this heavy feeder's nutrient needs.
items.description: Apodanthera is a genus of plants in the family Cucurbitaceae. It includes 25 species native to the southwestern United States, Mexico, and South America from Ecuador and eastern Brazil to northern Argentina.

items.name: Hanburia spectabilis
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep in peat-free compost, keeping them at 20C to prevent rotting.
Plant out in late May after frosts, spacing vines 90cm apart against a sturdy south-facing trellis.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly in dry spells, keeping the climbing foliage completely dry.
Pinch out the main growing tip at 1.8m to encourage lateral fruiting branches to form in July.
Protect young spring shoots from slugs using beer traps or copper tape around the support posts.
items.description:
Hanburia may refer to:Hanburia (plant), a genus of plants in the family Cucurbitaceae
Hanburia (trilobite), a genus of trilobites in the order Corynexochida

items.name: Telfairia occidentalis
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at three centimetres deep in pots using a heated propagator at 21C.
Grow in a greenhouse or south-facing polytunnel to survive the cool and wet UK summer climate.
Water the base deeply twice a week to keep soil moist but never waterlogged to prevent root rot.
Provide a sturdy trellis or netting by June to support the heavy, vigorous climbing vines.
Harvest young tender leaves and shoots regularly to encourage bushier growth and more foliage.
items.description: Telfairia occidentalis is a tropical vine grown in West Africa as a leaf vegetable and for its edible seeds. Common names for the plant include fluted gourd, fluted pumpkin, ugu, "Eweroko" ,okwukwo-wiri, nkemaku in Ubang language, and ikong-ubong, "Akwukwor ri". T. occidentalis is a member of the family Cucurbitaceae and is indigenous to southern Nigeria. The fluted gourd grows in many nations of West Africa, but is mainly cultivated in southeastern Nigeria and it is used primarily in soups and herbal medicines. Although the fruit is inedible, the seeds produced by the gourd are high in protei

items.name: Hodgsonia heteroclita
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 25C in deep pots of free-draining compost to protect taproots.
Grow this vigorous climber exclusively in a heated greenhouse or conservatory to survive UK cold.
Water deeply at the base twice a week during summer, keeping the foliage dry to prevent mildew.
Provide a sturdy overhead trellis or wires to support the heavy, fast-growing woody vines.
Hand-pollinate the large nocturnal white flowers at dusk as UK night pollinators are absent.
items.description: Hodgsonia is a small genus of fruit-bearing vines in the family Cucurbitaceae.

items.name: Cucumber
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at two centimetres deep using pots placed on a heated seedling mat.
Water the soil deeply at the base of the plant to keep leaves dry and prevent powdery mildew.
Pinch out the main growing tip after five leaves develop to encourage productive side branches.
Remove all male flowers on greenhouse F1 cucumber varieties to prevent bitter-tasting fruits.
Plant alongside dill or marigolds to deter aphids and attract essential pollinators to flowers.
items.description: Cucumis is a genus of twining, tendril-bearing plants in the family Cucurbitaceae which includes the cucumber, true melons, the horned melon, and the West Indian gherkin.

items.name: Calycophysum pedunculatum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using a heated propagator to survive chilly UK springs.
Grow this vigorous climber against a south-facing brick wall to trap essential summer heat.
Water deeply at the base twice a week to keep soil moist without wetting the vulnerable foliage.
Prune the main vine in July once it reaches two meters to force lateral fruiting side shoots.
Watch for powdery mildew in damp August weather and space plants widely to improve air flow.
items.description: Calycophysum is a genus of the gourd family.

items.name: Sechium edule (Jacq.) Sw.
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in deep pots in March by burying the entire supermarket-bought fruit on its side.
Plant out in late May after frosts in a south-facing, sheltered spot with sturdy trellis support.
Water copiously at the base twice weekly during dry summer spells to prevent flower drop in August.
Mulch heavily with well-rotted manure in autumn to protect the tuberous roots from winter wet.
Prune lateral shoots back to four leaves in July to encourage female flowers and improve air flow.
items.description: Sechium was a genus of plants now subsumed into the genus Sicyos: also placed in the tribe Sicyoeae of the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae. Its best known member was the edible and widely cultivated chayote.

items.name: Buffalo gourd
items.growersTips:
Grow this wild squash in a large terracotta pot to restrict its massive invasive tuberous root system.
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using a heated propagator set to 21C to mimic desert heat.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot against a brick wall to maximize essential summer heat.
Water deeply only once a week during dry spells to prevent the taproot from rotting in wet UK soil.
Protect young vines from slugs in May using beer traps as damp UK springs threaten early growth.
items.description: Cucurbita foetidissima is a tuberous xerophytic plant found in the central and southwestern United States and northern Mexico. It has numerous common names, but is most commonly called the buffalo gourd in English. The type specimen was collected from Mexico by Alexander von Humboldt and Aimé Bonpland sometime before 1817. In Latin, foetidissima means most unpleasant smell.

items.name: Cucurbita argyrosperma
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep in 9cm pots using a heated propagator to combat cool UK springs
Plant out in June after frost into soil enriched with a full wheelbarrow of well-rotted manure
Water deeply at the base twice weekly in dry spells, keeping the large, hairy foliage entirely dry
Support the heavy Cushaw fruits on wooden boards or tiles to prevent rot from damp British soil
Harvest before the first autumn frost when the stem corks, then cure indoors at 20C for two weeks
items.description: Cucurbita argyrosperma, commonly known as cushaw, kershaw, or silver-seed gourd, is a species of squash grown most frequently in North and Central America, and believed to originate from southern Mexico. This annual herbaceous plant is cultivated for its nutritional value: its flowers, shoots, and fruits are all harvested, but it is cultivated commonly in its native range for seeds.

items.name: Fig-leaf gourd
items.growersTips:
Sow indoors in April at 2cm deep using individual 9cm pots to protect from late UK spring frosts.
Plant out in late May after hardening off, spacing at least 2 metres apart to allow for huge growth.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly in dry summer spells, keeping the dense foliage completely dry.
Prune the vigorous main vines in late August to channel energy into ripening the existing green fruit.
Harvest in October before the first autumn frost, leaving a 5cm stem to prevent rot during storage.
items.description: Cucurbita ficifolia is a species of squash, grown for its edible seeds, fruit, and greens. It has common names including black seed squash, chilacayote, cidra, fig-leaf gourd, and Malabar gourd. This species is grown widely from Argentina and Chile to Mexico. It is also cultivated in regions of the world including India, Japan, Korea, China, the Philippines, Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, and Angola.

items.name: Luffa operculata
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using a heated propagator set to 25C to ensure germination.
Grow in a greenhouse or south-facing polytunnel to provide the high heat this tropical vine needs.
Water daily at the base with tepid water to keep soil moist but prevent stem rot in cool UK summers.
Train the vigorous vines onto sturdy vertical trellises to keep the heavy fruit off damp soil.
Harvest the small sponge-like gourds in autumn as soon as the outer skin turns yellow and dry.
items.description: Luffa operculata is a species of Luffa native to South and Central America. It is cultivated for its fruit, which when fully ripe is strongly fibrous and is used as a fibrous scrubbing sponge for household cleaning. The fruit is a capsule with spikes. The fruit is dark-brown when mature. It is also grown in gardens and yards as an ornamental plant. In colder places they can be grown indoors as a houseplant.

items.name: Cucurbita palmata
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep in 9cm pots using a heated propagator set to 21C.
Plant out in June after the last frost into soil enriched with plenty of well-rotted manure.
Water deeply at the base twice a week during dry spells, keeping the rough, hairy foliage dry.
Protect young plants from slugs using beer traps or copper tape until the stems become woody.
Grow in the sunniest south-facing spot possible to help this desert species ripen fruit in UK heat.
items.description: Cucurbita palmata is a species of flowering plant in the squash family known by the common names coyote melon and coyote gourd. It is similar to Cucurbita californica, Cucurbita cordata, Cucurbita cylindrata, and Cucurbita digitata and all these species hybridize readily. It was first identified by Sereno Watson in 1876. These species form the only restricted xerophyte species group in the genus Cucurbita. Each member of this species group is native to the Southwestern United States and Northwestern Mexico where they are relatively uncommon. Each group member is found in hot, arid regions with

items.name: Ash gourd
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep using a heated propagator to maintain the required 22C.
Grow plants inside a greenhouse or polytunnel to ensure the high heat and humidity they need to fruit.
Hand-pollinate the yellow flowers midday using a paintbrush as UK pollinator activity can be low.
Support the heavy gourds with netting slings attached to a sturdy trellis to prevent vine breakage.
Restrict watering as fruits mature in late August to help the protective waxy white coating develop.
items.description: Benincasa hispida, the wax gourd, also called ash gourd, white gourd, winter gourd, winter melon, tallow gourd, ash pumpkin, dongah or Chinese preserving melon, is a species of vine.

items.name: Sicyos macrophyllus
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at a depth of two centimeters using bottom heat to combat cool UK springs
Plant out in late May after the last frost in moisture-retentive soil enriched with well-rotted manure
Provide a sturdy trellis or archway to support the rapid growth of these vigorous climbing vines
Water deeply at the base twice a week during dry summer spells to prevent powdery mildew on leaves
Monitor vines weekly in June for slugs and snails which target the tender young growing tips
items.description: Sicyos macrophyllus is a rare species of flowering plant in the Cucurbitaceae, the squash family. It is endemic to Hawaii where it is present only on the island of Hawaii. It has likely been extirpated from the island of Maui. Common names include alpine bur cucumber, largeleaf bur-cucumber, and 'anunu.

items.name: Cyclanthera pedata
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at two centimetres deep using individual pots to protect fragile roots.
Plant out in late May after frosts pass, choosing a south-facing wall to maximise UK summer heat.
Provide a sturdy two-metre trellis or netting immediately to support their rapid, self-clinging vines.
Water copiously at the base during July and August dry spells to prevent the small fruits dropping.
Harvest the Achocha pods when five centimetres long before the seeds harden and turn black inside.
items.description: Cyclanthera is a genus of flowering plants in the family Cucurbitaceae. The name comes from the fact that some species show extreme cases of stamen fusion forming a ring around the gynoecium, with a single locule.

items.name: Luffa aegyptiaca
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep using a heated propagator to ensure the required 21C for germ.
Grow luffas in a greenhouse or polytunnel as UK summers are too cold and wet for outdoor success.
Pinch out the main growing tip when it reaches 1.5m to encourage side shoots where fruit will form.
Water daily at the base to keep soil moist but keep leaves dry to prevent powdery mildew attacks.
Hand-pollinate the yellow female flowers using a small paintbrush to guarantee fruit set in the UK.
items.description: Luffa is a genus of tropical and subtropical vines in the pumpkin, squash and gourd family (Cucurbitaceae).

items.name: Bryony black
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in autumn in cold frames as they need winter chill to break dormancy before spring growth.
Plant tubers fifteen centimetres deep in well-drained, chalky soil to mimic their native UK habitat.
Provide a sturdy trellis or allow them to scramble through established hedges for natural support.
Water deeply once a week during dry summer spells, keeping the crown dry to prevent winter rot.
Wear thick gloves when pruning in autumn because all parts of this native vine are highly toxic.
items.description: Bryonia is a genus of flowering plants in the gourd family. Bryony is its best-known common name. They are native to western Eurasia and adjacent regions, such as North Africa, the Canary Islands and South Asia.

items.name: Luffa aegyptiaca
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep using a heated propagator to ensure the required 21C for germ.
Grow in a greenhouse or south-facing polytunnel as UK summers are too cold for outdoor success.
Provide a sturdy trellis and hand-pollinate the yellow flowers daily using a soft artist brush.
Water copiously at the base daily once fruit sets and feed weekly with high-potassium tomato food.
Harvest in October when the skin turns yellow-brown and feels light before the first autumn frosts.
items.description: Luffa aegyptiaca, the sponge gourd, Egyptian cucumber or Vietnamese luffa, is an annual species of vine cultivated for its fruit, native to South and Southeast Asia.

items.name: Native briony
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at a depth of two centimeters using a heated propagator set to twenty-one Celsius.
Grow this tender climber inside a greenhouse or conservatory to guarantee the heat needed for fruiting.
Water the base deeply twice a week to keep the soil consistently moist but never waterlogged.
Provide a sturdy trellis or netting at planting time to support the vigorous climbing tendrils.
Watch for powdery mildew in late summer and improve ventilation around the foliage to prevent it.
items.description: Diplocyclos palmatus is a vine in the family Cucurbitaceae. It is commonly known as native bryony or striped cucumber. In Marathi, it is called shivlingi due to its seed which resembles a lingam.

items.name: Cucurbita moschata
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep on their sides in 9cm pots to prevent rotting in cold UK soil.
Plant out in late May after frosts into soil enriched with a bucket of well-rotted manure per plant.
Water deeply at the base not the leaves, aiming for 10 litres per plant weekly during dry summer spells.
Pinch out the main growing tip at 2 metres long in July to force energy into developing female flowers.
Elevate swelling fruits onto bricks or tiles by August to stop damp UK soil from rotting the skins.
items.description: Cucurbita moschata is a species originating in the tropical Americas which is cultivated for edible flesh, flowers, greens, and seeds. It includes cultivars known in English as squash or pumpkin. Cultivars of C. moschata are generally more tolerant of hot, humid weather than squash of other domesticated species. C. moschata also exhibit a greater resistance to certain disease and insects, notably including to the squash vine borer. Commercially-made pumpkin pie mix is most often made from varieties of C. moschata.

items.name: Chayote
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using peat-free compost to avoid late UK spring frosts
Plant out in late May against a sturdy trellis to support the vigorous climbing vines in wet wind
Water deeply at the base twice a week during dry summer spells to prevent powdery mildew on leaves
Pinch out the growing tips in July to restrict rampant spread and encourage lateral fruiting side-shoots
Hand-pollinate the small greenish flowers in dull UK summers to guarantee successful fruit set
items.description: Sicyos is a flowering plant genus of the family Cucurbitaceae. Members of the genus may be known as burr cucumbers, but the genus includes Sicyos edulis which is the christophine or chayote.

items.name: Lagenaria sphaerica
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool UK spring soils.
Plant out in June against a south-facing wall in soil enriched with well-rotted manure for warmth.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly to keep soil moist but avoid wetting leaves to prevent mildew.
Pinch out the main growing tip at 2 metres to encourage lateral fruiting branches in short summers.
Hand-pollinate the white evening flowers using a paintbrush as UK nocturnal pollinators are scarce.
items.description: Lagenaria sphaerica is a herbaceous climber in the family Cucurbitaceae. It is commonly known as the wild melon.

items.name: Lagenaria rufa
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using bottom heat of 21C to counter cool UK spring soils.
Plant out in June against a south-facing wall in soil enriched with plenty of well-rotted manure.
Water deeply at the base twice weekly in dry spells, keeping the hairy foliage completely dry.
Pinch out the main vine tip at two metres in July to force side shoots where female flowers form.
Hand-pollinate the nocturnal white flowers at dusk using a soft brush to ensure fruit set in the UK.
items.description: Lagenaria rufa is a flowering plant in the family Cucurbitaceae. It is a climbing vine. Its flowers range from white to yellow. The fruit is a gourd, dark green when developing but becomes cream-orange when ripe. It is native to Western Africa.

items.name: Silk gourd
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 2cm depth using a heated propagator to overcome the cool UK spring.
Grow in a greenhouse or against a south-facing wall in fertile soil with a high-potassium feed.
Train the vigorous vines up strong trellises and pinch out the main growing tip at two metres.
Hand-pollinate the yellow evening-opening flowers using a paintbrush to ensure fruit set in the UK.
Harvest when fruits are 15cm long for eating or leave until the skin turns yellow-brown for sponges.
items.description: Luffa acutangula is a cucurbitaceous vine commercially grown for its unripe fruits as a vegetable. Mature fruits are used as natural cleaning sponges. Its fruit slightly resembles a cucumber or zucchini with ridges. It is native to South Asia and has been naturalised in other regions. It is also grown as a houseplant in places with colder climates. English common English names include angled luffa, Chinese okra, dish cloth gourd, ridged gourd, sponge gourd, vegetable gourd, strainer vine, ribbed loofah, silky gourd, and silk gourd.

items.name: Cucurbita maxima
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April 1.5cm deep on their sides in 9cm pots to prevent rotting in wet UK soil.
Plant out in late May after frosts, burying the stem up to the first leaves to encourage extra roots.
Water deeply at the base, not the leaves, to prevent powdery mildew in humid UK summer weather.
Place a slate or tile under developing pumpkins in August to stop them rotting on damp British soil.
Pinch out growing tips in late August so the plant puts all energy into ripening existing fruits.
items.description: Cucurbita maxima, one of at least five species of cultivated squash, is one of the most diverse domesticated species. This species originated in South America from the wild subspecies Cucurbita maxima subsp. andreana over 4,000 years ago. Cucurbita maxima, known for modern varieties as Hubbard, Delicious, Marblehead, Boston Marrow, and Turks Turban, originated in northern Argentina near the Andes or in certain Andean valleys. Secondary centers of diversity include India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and the southern Appalachians.

items.name: Calabash
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in April at 2cm deep on their sides in pots to prevent rot before planting out.
Plant out in late May after frosts in soil enriched with plenty of well-rotted manure or compost.
Hand-pollinate the white evening-opening flowers using a paintbrush to ensure successful fruit set.
Provide a strong trellis or support frame to keep the heavy gourds off the damp UK soil and clean.
Water deeply at the base twice a week during dry spells, keeping the foliage dry to avoid mildew.
items.description: Calabash, also known as bottle gourd, white-flowered gourd, long melon, birdhouse gourd, New Guinea bean, New Guinea butter bean, Tasmania bean, zucca melon and opo squash, is a vine which is grown for its fruit. It belongs to the family Cucurbitaceae, is native to tropical Africa, and cultivated across the tropics. It can be either harvested young to be consumed as a vegetable, or harvested mature to be dried and used as a kitchen utensil, beverage container or a musical instrument. When it is fresh, the fruit has a light green smooth skin and white flesh.

items.name: Great Fringed-Flower Vine
items.growersTips:
Start seeds indoors in April at 20C in deep pots to protect the taproot before late May planting.
Grow against a south-facing wall under glass or polytunnel to meet the high heat demand in the UK.
