items.description: Persicaria amphibia is a species of flowering plant in the knotweed family known by several common names, including longroot smartweed, water knotweed, water smartweed, and amphibious bistort. It is native to much of North America, Asia, Europe, and parts of Africa, and it grows elsewhere as an introduced species and sometimes a noxious weed.

items.name: Persicaria hydropiper
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring in consistently boggy soil or pond margins where they will never dry out.
Control its aggressive self-seeding by cutting back the pinkish flower spikes before autumn.
Plant alongside water mint or marsh marigold to balance its invasive spreading root habit.
Grow this pungent herb in partial shade to keep the peppery leaves tender for culinary use.
Wear gloves when weeding to avoid skin irritation from the plant's highly acrid sap.
items.description: Persicaria hydropiper, also known as water pepper, marshpepper knotweed, arse smart or tade, is a plant of the family Polygonaceae. A widespread species, Persicaria hydropiper is found in Australia, New Zealand, temperate Asia, Europe and North America. The plant grows in damp places and shallow water. Cultivated varieties are eaten in East Asia for their pungent flavor.

items.name: Rumex azoricus
items.growersTips:
Plant this moisture-loving dock in deep, humus-rich soil that mimics its native Azores bog habitat.
Position in partial shade to protect the large leaves from scorching in dry UK summer spells.
Water copiously during dry summer weeks to keep the soil consistently damp and prevent leaf wilt.
Cut back the spent flower spikes in late summer to prevent aggressive self-seeding around the garden.
Watch for dock beetles and slugs which quickly shred the ornamental foliage in damp spring weather.
items.description: Rumex azoricus is a species of sorrel in the family Polygonaceae. It is endemic to the Azores, Portugal.

items.name: Hollisteria lanata
items.growersTips:
Grow this rare annual in sharply draining sandy loam to mimic its native dry California habitat.
Sow seeds shallowly under glass in early spring as UK damp will rot them if sown directly outdoors.
Position in your sunniest south-facing border or gravel garden to maximize essential summer heat.
Water sparingly only during prolonged dry spells, allowing the soil to dry out completely between.
Protect young plants from slugs and snails which eagerly target the tender woolly foliage in spring.
items.description: Hollisteria is a genus of plants in the family Polygonaceae with a single species, Hollisteria lanata. It is endemic to California. It is known by the common name false spikeflower.

items.name: Common knotweed
items.growersTips:
Hand-weed young seedlings in late spring before their deep, tough taproot anchors in compacted soil.
Sow seeds in autumn in heavy clay or gravelly paths where other plants fail to tolerate foot traffic.
Avoid watering once established as this weed-like annual thrives in dry, baked UK summer soils.
Hoe the prostrate stems weekly in June to prevent the plant from setting its highly abundant seeds.
Grow alongside Plantago major in high-traffic garden paths as they share a tolerance for compaction.
items.description: Polygonum arenastrum, commonly known as equal-leaved knotgrass, is a summer annual flowering plant in the knotweed family Polygonaceae. Other common names include common knotweed, prostrate knotweed, mat grass, oval-leaf knotweed, stone grass, wiregrass, and door weed, as well as many others. It is native to Eurasia and can be found on other continents as an introduced species and a common noxious weed. Knotweed was first seen in North America in 1809 and is now seen across much of the United States and Canada.

items.name: Polygonum cognatum
items.growersTips:
Plant in gritty, free-draining soil to prevent winter root rot during wet UK winters.
Position in full sun to mimic its native Turkish hillsides and encourage tight, prostrate growth.
Water sparingly once established, allowing the soil to dry out completely between applications.
Propagate by dividing the woody rootstock in early spring just as new green shoots emerge.
Grow alongside Thymus serpyllum or Sedum album to create a drought-tolerant, low-maintenance carpet.
items.description: Polygonum cognatum, commonly called Indian knotgrass or madimak, is an edible weedy creeping perennial herb in the genus Polygonum, frequently eaten by people of Turkey. It has larger leaves than most other species of Polygonum.

items.name: Polygonum coccineum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring at a depth of 5mm into moist, peat-free compost using a heated propagator.
Keep the soil consistently wet by watering daily to mimic its natural UK wetland habitat.
Position in full sun to partial shade in heavy clay or poorly drained boggy garden borders.
Pinch out the growing tips in early summer to encourage a bushier habit and more pink flower spikes.
Watch for aphids and snails on young spring shoots and clear debris to prevent overwintering pests.
items.description: Persicaria amphibia is a species of flowering plant in the knotweed family known by several common names, including longroot smartweed, water knotweed, water smartweed, and amphibious bistort. It is native to much of North America, Asia, Europe, and parts of Africa, and it grows elsewhere as an introduced species and sometimes a noxious weed.

items.name: Chorizanthe brevicornu
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring at a depth of 2mm in a gritty, sharply draining soil mix to prevent root rot.
Grow in containers under a cold frame to protect this desert annual from excessive UK winter wet.
Water sparingly only when the top 5cm of soil is bone dry, mimicking its native arid habitat.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot of your garden to maximize limited UK summer heat.
Sow alongside Sedums in rockeries to provide the ultra-dry, low-nutrient soil conditions it needs.
items.description: Chorizanthe brevicornu is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family which is known by the common name brittle spineflower. It is native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico, where it is widely distributed but is most abundant in the deserts. The plant extends an erect, naked, highly branching stem which is greenish in color. Most of the leaves grow from the base of the plant, but a few small ones may appear up on the stem. At the end of each of the many branches is a tube-shaped inflorescence which opens into a tiny white or greenish-yellow flower a few millimeters

items.name: Chorizanthe douglasii
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in autumn using a cold frame to mimic winter chill.
Grow in a gritty, sharply draining soil mix with added perlite to survive wet UK winter rot.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is dry, keeping foliage dry to prevent mildew.
Position in the brightest, south-facing spot of your garden to maximise limited UK summer sun.
Plant alongside low-growing sedums or thymes which share its need for dry, nutrient-poor soil.
items.description: Chorizanthe douglasii is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common names San Benito spineflower and Douglas' spineflower. It is endemic to California, where it grows in the mountains of the Southern California Coast Ranges, from the Santa Lucia Range east to the Gabilan Range.

items.name: Wrinkled spineflower
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in April under glass at a depth of two millimetres using a gritty, free-draining compost
Grow in terracotta pots placed in full sun to mimic its native arid habitat and prevent root rot
Water sparingly from below only when the soil is dry to the touch, keeping the foliage bone dry
Mix fifty percent horticultural grit into peat-free compost to ensure the rapid drainage it needs
Protect young plants from slugs and snails using copper tape around pots during wet UK spring days
items.description: Chorizanthe corrugata is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name wrinkled spineflower. It is native to the Mojave and Sonoran Deserts of the southwestern United States and two states of northwest Mexico, Baja California and Sonora.

items.name: Chorizanthe cuspidata
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in early spring using a cold frame to protect them
Grow in a sharply draining sandy loam mix with added grit to mimic its native coastal dune habitat
Water sparingly only when the top five centimetres of soil is dry to prevent root rot in wet UK summers
Position in your sunniest south-facing border or gravel garden to maximise essential light levels
Plant alongside low-growing sedums or thrift to provide structural support for its sprawling stems
items.description: Chorizanthe cuspidata is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name San Francisco spineflower. It is endemic to California, where it is known only from the San Francisco Bay Area and to the immediate north and south. It grows in sandy coastal habitat.

items.name: Chorizanthe membranacea
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at two millimetres deep in autumn under cold frames to survive wet UK winters.
Grow in a gritty, free-draining soil mix with fifty percent horticultural sand to prevent root rot.
Water sparingly only when the top five centimetres of soil is dry, mimicking dry California summers.
Position pots in the brightest south-facing spot to maximise sunlight during short UK summer days.
Watch for slugs and snails on young spring shoots as damp UK weather makes them highly vulnerable.
items.description: Chorizanthe membranacea is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name pink spineflower. It is native to Oregon and California, where it is widespread and in some areas quite common. It can be found in a wide variety of habitats.

items.name: Chorizanthe fimbriata
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly in autumn under glass to mimic its native dry winter cycle before spring planting
Grow in a gritty scree bed or terracotta pots with fifty percent grit to survive wet UK winters
Water only when the top three inches of soil are dry to prevent root rot in damp British climates
Position in the most sun-baked south-facing spot in your garden to encourage the pink fringed blooms
Plant alongside hardy sedums and sempervivums which share its extreme drought and drainage needs
items.description: Chorizanthe fimbriata, the fringed spineflower, is an annual plant in the family Polygonaceae, the buckwheats. It is a member of the genus Chorizanthe, the spineflowers, and is native to southern California and northern Baja California.

items.name: Chorizanthe parryi
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly in autumn under a cold frame to mimic winter wet then dry out for spring planting.
Grow in a gritty mix of five parts sharp sand to one part loam to survive wet UK winter dampness.
Water only when the top three inches of soil are bone dry to prevent root rot in humid UK summers.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot or gravel garden to maximise scarce UK summer heat.
Protect young spring shoots from slugs using copper tape as damp UK weather brings heavy infestations.
items.description: Chorizanthe parryi is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name Parry's spineflower and San Bernardino spineflower.

items.name: Chorizanthe orcuttiana
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in autumn on the soil surface of a sharply draining, gritty, low-nutrient sandy mix.
Grow in pots under a cold frame to protect this winter-annual from excessive UK winter wetness.
Water sparingly from below only when the soil dries completely, mimicking its arid native habitat.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot possible to maximise scarce UK summer warmth and light.
Avoid all fertilisers as high nutrient levels will quickly kill this specialized coastal plant.
items.description: Chorizanthe orcuttiana is a rare small annual plant in the buckwheat family, Polygonaceae. It is known commonly as Orcutt's spineflower or the San Diego spineflower, and it is endemic to San Diego County, California. The plant is diminutive, and a hand-lens is necessary for proper identification. The plant is very sensitive to temperature and precipitation, and under drought or hot conditions the seeds will not germinate or survive. The plant is visible anywhere from February through July during good rain year, but most years the plant is only visible from April to June. Each minute flower yie

items.name: Chorizanthe pungens
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in autumn in well-drained sandy soil to mimic its native dry Mediterranean-style habitat.
Grow in terracotta pots with a grit-heavy compost mix to ensure the roots never sit in UK winter wet.
Place in the sunniest south-facing spot of your garden to maximise warmth and prevent damping off.
Water sparingly only during prolonged dry summer spells, allowing the gritty soil to dry out fully.
Position near low-growing Sedums to provide physical support and prevent wind damage to weak stems.
items.description: Chorizanthe pungens is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name Monterey spineflower. It is endemic to California, where it is known from the San Francisco Bay Area south along the Central Coast.

items.name: Chorizanthe staticoides
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly in autumn under a cold frame to survive wet UK winters before spring planting.
Grow in a mix of three parts grit to one part peat-free compost to mimic dry native scree soils.
Water only during prolonged dry spring spells, allowing the gritty growing medium to dry fully.
Position in your sunniest south-facing border or gravel garden to maximise scarce UK summer heat.
Plant alongside low-growing Sedums or Thymus which share its need for sharp drainage and low nutrients.
items.description: Chorizanthe staticoides is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name Turkish rugging. It is endemic to California, where it is a common member of the flora in the chaparral and scrub habitats in a number of regions.

items.name: Chorizanthe robusta
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring at a depth of three millimetres in a free-draining sandy loam to prevent rot.
Place in the sunniest south-facing spot to mimic its native California dunes in the damp UK climate.
Water sparingly only during prolonged dry spells once established as this annual hates wet roots.
Sow directly into final pots to avoid transplant shock which easily kills its delicate taproot.
Protect young seedlings from slugs and snails using copper tape around pots during wet UK springs.
items.description: Chorizanthe robusta is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family. It is endemic to California, where it is a rare, federally listed endangered species.

items.name: Chorizanthe valida
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at two millimetres depth in autumn using a gritty, free-draining compost mix.
Position pots in a south-facing cold frame to protect overwintering seedlings from heavy UK rain.
Water sparingly from below only when the top two centimetres of soil has dried out completely.
Grow in containers of pure horticultural grit and peat-free compost to mimic native sandy soils.
Place copper tape around pots to protect the delicate young foliage from nocturnal slug damage.
items.description: Chorizanthe valida is a rare species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name Sonoma spineflower. It is endemic to West Marin, Marin County, California, where it is known from only one remaining natural population at Point Reyes National Seashore. It was thought to be extinct until 1980 when the Point Reyes population was discovered.

items.name: Chorizanthe watsonii
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in autumn using cold frames to mimic winter chill.
Grow in a sharply draining mix of five parts grit to one part loam to prevent winter wet root rot.
Water sparingly only when the top five centimetres of soil is dry to mimic its native arid habitat.
Position in the brightest south-facing spot or unheated greenhouse to maximise scarce UK sunlight.
Plant alongside low-growing Sedums which share its need for dry soil and won't crowd its tiny frame.
items.description: Chorizanthe watsonii is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name Fivetooth Spineflower or Watson's Spineflower. They are an annual herb native to the western United States including Idaho, California, Oregon, Nevada, Utah, Washington and Arizona, namely the Mojave Desert which runs through many of them.

items.name: Chorizanthe stellulata
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in autumn using a cold frame to mimic winter chill.
Grow in a sharply draining gritty soil mix to prevent root rot during wet UK winters and springs.
Water sparingly only when the top five centimetres of soil is dry to replicate its arid habitat.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot of your garden to maximise limited UK summer warmth.
Plant alongside low-growing sedums or sempervivums which share its need for dry, nutrient-poor soil.
items.description: Chorizanthe stellulata is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name starlet spineflower. It is endemic to California, where it grows in the dry woodlands of the low mountains and foothills along the central part of the state, such as the Sierra Nevada foothills. The plant takes an erect form, reaching up to 30 centimeters tall. The leaves are located at the base of the plant, and there is also a whorl of leaves at mid-stem. The inflorescence is a dense cluster of flowers, each flower surrounded by hairy, bristly white bracts tipped with hooked awns. The flow

items.name: Chorizanthe uniaristata
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in April under glass in a gritty, free-draining compost mix at a depth of just two millimetres
Water sparingly only when the top two inches of soil are dry to prevent root rot in damp UK weather
Position in the sunniest south-facing border or gravel garden to mimic its dry native habitat
Grow in terracotta pots alongside Sedums to easily move them shelter during heavy autumn downpours
Watch for slugs and snails on young spring seedlings as damp UK gardens pose a high risk to shoots
items.description: Chorizanthe uniaristata is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae known by the common name one-awn spineflower. It is endemic to central California, where it is known from several of the local mountain ranges, as well as the Central Coast.

items.name: Chorizanthe xanti
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring at a depth of three millimetres in a free-draining sandy loam to prevent rot.
Water sparingly only when the top five centimetres of soil is dry to mimic its native arid habitat.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot or under a cold frame to protect from wet UK summers.
Grow in terracotta pots with added grit to ensure rapid drainage and prevent winter waterlogging.
Sow alongside drought-tolerant Sedum or Festuca glauca which share its strict low-water needs.
items.description: Chorizanthe xanti is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name Riverside spineflower. It is endemic to California, where it grows in several of the mountain ranges from the Sierra Nevada to the Southern California Transverse Ranges in forest, woodland, and scrub habitats.

items.name: Rumex triangulivalvis
items.growersTips:
Plant this willow dock in moist, poorly drained clay or boggy soil near UK garden ponds or streams.
Sow seeds in spring just below the soil surface at a depth of two millimetres in cold frames.
Control its aggressive spreading habit by planting it in submerged containers to restrict roots.
Cut back the spent flower spikes in late summer to prevent heavy self-seeding across your lawn.
Watch for dock beetles in May and handpick them to protect the narrow, willow-like foliage.
items.description: Rumex triangulivalvis is a species of flowering plant belonging to the family Polygonaceae.

items.name: Polygonum oxyspermum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly in early spring using a free-draining sandy grit mix to mimic coastal shingle
Water sparingly once established to replicate dry beach soils and prevent root rot in damp UK winters
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot to provide the high light levels this coastal native needs
Grow alongside sea kale or thrift in gravel gardens to match its natural seaside habitat preferences
Check regularly for slugs during wet British springs as young fleshy shoots are highly vulnerable
items.description: Polygonum oxyspermum is a coastal species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family. It is native to Europe, primarily along the shores of the Atlantic, the North Sea, and the Baltic Sea, from France and Ireland to Finland and Russia. It is also naturalized in eastern Canada and in the US State of Maine.

items.name: Polygonum erectum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in March to benefit from cool UK spring rains.
Grow in compacted, heavy clay soils near pathways where other delicate annuals struggle to survive.
Water young seedlings weekly during dry spells, then leave established plants to rely on UK rainfall.
Watch for dock leaf beetles in June and handpick them to prevent severe defoliation of the crop.
Pull up the shallow roots in late August before the green flowers drop seeds to control self-sowing.
items.description: Polygonum erectum, commonly called erect knotweed, is a North American species of herbaceous plant in the buckwheat family (Polygonaceae). It is found primarily in the northeastern and north-central parts of the United States, but with scattered populations in other parts of the US and also in Canada.

items.name: Persicaria posumbu
items.growersTips:
Plant in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade to mimic its native woodland edge habitat.
Water consistently during dry UK summer spells to keep the soil evenly damp but not waterlogged.
Divide the root clumps in early spring just as new growth begins to propagate and control spread.
Protect young spring shoots from slugs and snails using organic grit barriers or beer traps.
Cut back the faded foliage to ground level in late autumn after the first frost to tidy the clump.
items.description: Persicaria posumbu is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae. It was first described as Polygonum posumbu in 1825 and transferred to the genus Persicaria in 1919. Plants of the World Online records it as having a discontinuous native distribution: the Assam region, Bangladesh and the eastern Himalayas to the west, and Japan, Korea, the Kuril Islands and Primorye to the east.

items.name: Persicaria runcinata
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive, humus-rich soil in partial shade to keep the leaf chevron patterns vivid.
Water weekly during dry UK summers to prevent the shallow root system from drying out and wilting.
Divide the spreading clumps in early spring to control its vigorous spread and maintain plant vigor.
Protect emerging spring shoots from slugs and snails using organic grit barriers or beer traps.
Grow alongside hostas and ferns in damp woodland borders to complement its metallic foliage tones.
items.description: Persicaria runcinata is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native from the Himalayas east through mainland China to Taiwan and south to Java and the Philippines. It was first described in 1825 as Polygonum runcinata.

items.name: Acanthoscyphus parishii
items.growersTips:
Plant this California native in extremely gritty, free-draining soil to survive wet UK winters.
Grow in a terracotta pot to control moisture and move under a cold frame or porch during winter.
Water sparingly from below only when the soil is bone dry, keeping the crown completely dry.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot of your garden to mimic its hot desert habitat.
Surround the plant base with a thick layer of granite grit to prevent rot from damp UK soil.
items.description: Acanthoscyphus is a monotypic genus in the family Polygonaceae that contains the single species Acanthoscyphus parishii, which is sometimes called Parish's oxytheca. This species is native and endemic to southern California.

items.name: Willow weed
items.growersTips:
Plant in damp clay or boggy soil near UK ponds at a depth equal to the original nursery pot size.
Water heavily during dry summer spells to mimic its natural British canal and riverbank habitat.
Watch for dock beetles in June and handpick them to prevent severe foliage damage in wet weather.
Cut stems back to ground level in late autumn after the first frost to keep the crown healthy.
Divide the root clump in early spring using a sharp spade to control its vigorous spreading habit.
items.description: Persicaria lapathifolia, known as pale persicaria, is a plant of the family Polygonaceae. It is considered to be native throughout most of the world, from arctic to tropical realms, except South America and Southern Africa. It is closely related to Persicaria maculosa and as such is considered a weed in Britain and Europe. Other common names for the plant include pale smartweed, curlytop knotweed, and willow weed. It is a species complex made up of a great many varying forms, sometimes considered varieties. The environment also has a strong influence on the morphology of an individual plant.

items.name: Persicaria microcephala
items.growersTips:
Plant Red Dragon in moisture-retentive, humus-rich soil to prevent leaf scorch in dry UK summers.
Position in partial shade to maintain the vibrant purple and silver leaf variegation of Red Dragon.
Water deeply once a week during dry spells to keep the soil consistently damp but not waterlogged.
Cut back the dead stems to ground level in late autumn or early spring to encourage fresh growth.
Propagate by division in spring or take softwood cuttings in summer to increase your stock easily.
items.description: Persicaria microcephala, the small-headed knotweed, is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae. It is native to the Himalayas, and central and southern China, and it has been introduced to Great Britain. Its cultivar 'Red Dragon' has gained the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.

items.name: Persicaria elatior
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive clay or loam in partial shade to mimic its native damp woodland edge.
Water deeply during dry UK summer spells to keep the soil consistently damp and prevent leaf scorch.
Divide the congested root clumps in early spring just as new growth begins to propagate and renew.
Cut the faded flower spikes and stems down to the ground in late autumn after the first frost.
Position near Astilbe or moisture-loving ferns which thrive in the same damp British soil conditions.
items.description: Persicaria elatior, commonly known as tall knotweed, is a species of flowering plant native to eastern Australia. It was one of eleven species selected for the Save a Species Walk campaign in April 2016; scientists walked 300 km to raise money for collection of seeds to be prepared and stored at the Australian PlantBank at the Australian Botanic Garden Mount Annan.

items.name: Persicaria extremiorientalis
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive clay or loam in partial shade to mimic its native woodland edge habitat.
Sow seeds in cold frames during autumn as they require winter chilling to break dormancy in the UK.
Water deeply twice a week during dry summer spells to keep the soil consistently damp but not soggy.
Cut back the dead foliage to ground level in late autumn to prevent self-seeding and tidy the crown.
Divide established clumps in early spring to control its vigorous spread and renew plant vigour.
items.description: Persicaria extremiorientalis, the east Asian smartweed, is a plant species in the buckwheat family, native to Japan, China, Korea, and far eastern Russia and introduced to the eastern United States where it is found from North Carolina to Massachusetts.

items.name: Persicaria filiformis
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive clay or loam enriched with leafmould to mimic UK woodland conditions.
Sow seeds in cold frames in autumn as they require winter chilling to break dormancy for spring.
Position in partial shade to prevent the variegated foliage of cultivars like Painters Palette from scorching.
Divide established clumps in spring to control self-seeding and maintain vigorous growth.
Watch for slugs and snails on fresh spring shoots and protect with organic grit barriers.
items.description: Persicaria filiformis is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native to the Kuril Islands, Japan, Korea, Myanmar, the Philippines and Vietnam. It was first described as Polygonum filiforme in 1784 by Carl Thunberg and transferred to the genus Persicaria in 1819 by Takenoshin Nakai. The species has been treated as the variety filiformis of Persicaria virginiana, a North American species. The leaves are light green, eliptical, and about 15 cm (5.9 in) long. They are commonly marked with a pair of brown spots near the center of the leaf.

items.name: Polygonum douglasii
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of 2mm in early spring using free-draining sandy loam soil.
Position in full sun with poor soil to prevent floppy growth and encourage a compact habit.
Water sparingly once established as this annual prefers dry conditions and dislikes waterlogging.
Watch for slugs on young spring seedlings and protect them using grit barriers or organic pellets.
Allow the plant to self-seed naturally in autumn to ensure a display for the following year.
items.description: Polygonum douglasii is a species of flowering plant in the knotweed family known by the common name Douglas's knotweed. It is native to much of northern and western North America, where it can be found in many types of habitat, including disturbed areas. It has been found in Canada from British Columbia north to Yukon and east as far as Québec, and in the United States as far south as California, New Mexico, Iowa, and New York.

items.name: Rheum australe
items.growersTips:
Plant in deep, moisture-retentive, fertile soil enriched with plenty of well-rotted manure or compost
Position in full sun or partial shade, ensuring the crown sits just at the soil surface level
Water copiously during dry summer spells to support the massive, dramatic leaf development
Apply a thick mulch of organic matter in autumn to protect the crown from severe UK winter wet
Watch for slugs and snails on emerging spring shoots and clear away dead winter foliage promptly
items.description: Rheum australe, synonym Rheum emodi, is a flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae. It is commonly known as Himalayan rhubarb, Indian rhubarb and Red-veined pie plant. It is a medicinal herb used in the Indian Unani system of medicine, and formerly in the European system of medicine where it was traded as Indian rhubarb. The plant is found in the sub-alpine and alpine Himalayas at an altitude of 4000 m.

items.name: Rumex britannica
items.growersTips:
Plant in heavy clay or boggy soil near UK garden ponds to mimic its natural wet fenland habitat.
Sow seeds in cold frames during autumn to allow natural winter stratification under UK conditions.
Keep the soil constantly saturated or submerged in up to fifteen centimetres of water year-round.
Cut back the dead flower spikes in late autumn to prevent aggressive self-seeding across lawns.
Watch for dock beetles in spring and handpick them to protect the large decorative green leaves.
items.description: Rumex britannica is a flowering plant species in the family Polygonaceae.(Buckwheat family) (perennial).

items.name: Persicaria punctata
items.growersTips:
Plant this moisture-lover in boggy soil or shallow pond margins up to ten centimetres deep.
Water daily during dry UK summers to maintain the constantly wet soil this native bog plant needs.
Divide the vigorous root clumps in early spring to control its spread and propagate new plants.
Cut back the frost-damaged foliage to ground level in late autumn after the first UK frosts.
Grow in containers sunk into wet borders to restrict its invasive rhizomatous spreading habit.
items.description: Persicaria punctata is a species of flowering plant in the knotweed family known by the common names dotted smartweed and dotted knotweed.

items.name: Persicaria nepalensis
items.growersTips:
Grow in damp partial shade alongside ferns and hostas to mimic its native cool Himalayan woodland.
Control its aggressive self-seeding in mild UK autumns by deadheading flowers before they set seed.
Plant shallowly in moisture-retentive acidic clay soil enriched with leafmould to prevent drying out.
Water weekly during dry summer spells to stop the soft foliage from wilting and scorching in the sun.
Divide congested clumps in early spring just as new shoots emerge to control spread and renew vigour.
items.description: Persicaria nepalensis is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native to eastern Africa, including Madagascar, and parts of Asia. It has been introduced elsewhere: parts of Europe, North America and northern South America. The species was first described as Polygonum nepalense by Carl Meissner in 1826, and transferred to Persicaria by Hugo Gross in 1913.

items.name: Rumex cristatus
items.growersTips:
Dig out the deep taproot in early spring using a spade to prevent regrowth in heavy clay soils.
Cut flowering stems to the ground in July before seeds disperse to stop aggressive self-seeding.
Apply a glyphosate-based weedkiller directly to leaves in late summer when nutrients move to roots.
Wear thick gloves when handling to avoid skin irritation from the coarse hairs on mature foliage.
Do not compost any root fragments or seed heads; burn them or use your council green waste bin.
items.description: Rumex cristatus, the Greek dock, is a species of perennial herb in the family Polygonaceae.

items.name: Persicaria attenuata
items.growersTips:
Plant this moisture-lover in boggy pond margins or wet clay soils, submerged no deeper than 10cm.
Water daily during dry UK summers to keep the soil consistently saturated and prevent leaf scorch.
Cut back the frost-damaged foliage to ground level in late autumn to keep the crown tidy for winter.
Divide the fibrous root clumps in early spring to control its spread and propagate new specimens.
Grow alongside Caltha palustris or Iris pseudacorus to create a balanced, native UK wetland display.
items.description: Persicaria attenuata is a species of flowering plant native to Australia and Asia. It typically grows in wet land or streams.

items.name: Pink bubble persicaria
items.growersTips:
Plant this pink knotweed in free-draining soil to prevent winter root rot in wet UK climates.
Water young plants weekly until established, then only during prolonged dry British summer spells.
Cut back frost-damaged foliage in early spring to encourage fresh bronze-leaved ground cover.
Watch for slugs and snails on tender new spring shoots, using beer traps or organic grit barriers.
Grow alongside blue-flowered Campanula or dwarf conifers to contrast the pink globe-like blooms.
items.description: Persicaria capitata, the pink-headed persicaria, pinkhead smartweed, pink knotweed, Japanese knotweed, or pink bubble persicaria, is an Asian species of plants in the genus Persicaria within the Polygonaceae family. It is native to Asia and grown as an ornamental in other countries. It has become naturalized in Australia, South Africa and a few scattered locations in the Americas.

items.name: Polygonella robusta
items.growersTips:
Plant this sandhill native in a raised bed of 70% coarse grit and 30% peat-free ericaceous compost.
Position in your sunniest south-facing border to mimic its native Florida scrub heat in UK summers.
Water only during prolonged dry spells in summer, keeping the crown completely dry during winter.
Protect from winter wet by placing a cloche over the plant from November through to late March.
Propagate by taking semi-ripe cuttings in late summer as this short-lived perennial rarely sets seed.
items.description:
Polygonella robusta, also known as Polygonum nesomii, is a shrubby perennial flowering plant in the buckwheat (Polygonaceae) family. It is endemic to the U.S. state of Florida where it is a member of the sandhill plant community. Common names for it include largeflower jointweed and 
sandhill wireweed. P. robusta produces an abundance of flowers that are surrounded by papery bracts which range in color from white and light pink to deep rose. After flowering, usually in October, the plant maintains a rosette of basal foliage through the winter.

items.name: Sorrel
items.growersTips:
Sow Rumex sanguineus seeds in spring at five millimetres deep in moisture-retentive, neutral soil.
Water container-grown sorrel twice weekly in dry UK summers to stop leaves turning bitter and tough.
Cut back flower spikes in July to prevent invasive self-seeding and encourage fresh salad leaves.
Watch for green dock beetles in May and handpick them to prevent skeletonisation of the foliage.
Divide established clumps in March using a sharp spade to maintain vigour and propagate new plants.
items.description: The docks and sorrels, genus Rumex, are a genus of about 200 species of annual, biennial, and perennial herbs in the buckwheat family, Polygonaceae. Members of this genus are common perennial herbs with a worldwide native distribution in temperate and subtropical climates.

items.name: Chorizanthe rigida
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in late spring under glass in a gritty, free-draining mix to prevent UK damp rot.
Keep watering to a bare minimum, letting the soil dry out completely between light mistings.
Position pots in the brightest, south-facing spot possible to mimic their native desert sun.
Grow in terracotta pots rather than open UK soil to ensure excellent drainage and root warmth.
Do not fertilise this plant, as nutrient-rich UK multi-purpose composts will cause it to collapse.
items.description: Chorizanthe rigida, with the common names of devil's spineflower, rigid spineflower, spiny-herb, rigid spiny-herb, is an annual plant in the family Polygonaceae the buckwheats. It is a member of the genus Chorizanthe, the spineflowers and is found in the southwestern United States and northwest Mexico, in the states of California, Nevada, Utah, Arizona, Baja California, and Sonora.

items.name: Persicaria orientalis
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in autumn or cold-stratify in the fridge for six weeks to break dormancy in UK climates.
Plant in moisture-retentive, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade to prevent leaf scorch.
Water deeply twice a week during dry summer spells to keep the soil consistently damp.
Stake the tall, hollow stems by mid-spring using hazel twigs to prevent wind damage in UK gales.
Deadhead spent pink tassels in late summer to prevent aggressive self-seeding across your borders.
items.description: Persicaria orientalis is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, known as kiss-me-over-the-garden-gate and princess-feather. It was first described, as Polygonum orientale, by Carl Linnaeus in 1753. It was transferred to the genus Persicaria by Édouard Spach in 1841. Its native distribution is unclear. As of April 2023, Kew's Plants of The World Online lists its native distribution as ranging from the Russian far east to Indochina, Malesia and Australia. It is widely cultivated and naturalized.

items.name: Yard knotweed
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring after the last frost, barely covering them with five millimetres of fine soil.
Keep the soil consistently moist but never waterlogged during dry spells in UK summer months.
Pinch out the growing tips of young plants in late May to encourage a bushier, more compact habit.
Watch for aphids and slugs on tender new growth, using organic barriers or beer traps in damp weather.
Clear dead annual plants completely in autumn to prevent excessive self-seeding across your borders.
items.description: Polygonum is a genus of about 130 species of flowering plants in the buckwheat and knotweed family Polygonaceae. Common names include knotweed and knotgrass. In the Middle English glossary of herbs Alphita, it was known as ars-smerte. There have been various opinions about how broadly the genus should be defined. For example, buckwheat has sometimes been included in the genus as Polygonum fagopyrum. Former genera such as Polygonella have been subsumed into Polygonum; other genera have been split off.

items.name: Rumex pseudonatronatus
items.growersTips:
Plant this moisture-loving dock in heavy clay or boggy soil near UK garden ponds to mimic its wild habitat.
Sow seeds in spring at a depth of 5mm in containers kept outdoors to benefit from natural UK chill.
Water deeply twice a week during dry summer spells to keep the soil consistently wet, never dry.
Cut back the flowering stems in late August before seed set to stop aggressive self-seeding in lawns.
Check foliage weekly in June for green dock beetles and handpick them to prevent severe defoliation.
items.description: Rumex pseudonatronatus, common name field dock or Finnish dock, is a plant species native to northern Europe and northern Asia, known from Asiatic and European Russia, China, Mongolia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Finland, Norway, Sweden, Belgium, Netherlands, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Belarus, etc. It is naturalized in much of Canada and to the north-central United States. It is known from every Canadian province from Québec to British Columbia, plus Yukon, North Dakota, South Dakota and Minnesota. It grows in wet and/or disturbed sites along stream banks, lake shores, roadsides, ditches

items.name: Polygonum minimum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in early spring once the risk of frost has passed
Grow in poor to moderately fertile well-drained sandy loam to prevent excessive leggy leaf growth
Water sparingly only during prolonged dry summer spells as this alpine annual dislikes wet roots
Position in full sun in a rock garden or gravel scree bed to mimic its natural subalpine habitat
Clear dead plants in autumn but leave seed heads intact to allow self-seeding for the next spring
items.description: Polygonum minimum is a species of flowering plant in the knotweed family known by the common name broadleaf knotweed. It is native to much of western North America where it can be found in mountainous regions. It grows in the subalpine and alpine climates of high mountain ranges from Alaska to Arizona and New Mexico.

items.name: Polygonum paronychia
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring at a depth of 5mm in free-draining sandy loam to mimic UK coastal dunes.
Water young plants weekly until established, then only during prolonged dry summer spells.
Grow in full sun and poor soil to prevent this sprawling annual from becoming leggy and weak.
Watch for slugs and snails on tender spring seedlings, using organic grit barriers to protect them.
Sow alongside Armeria maritima in gravel gardens to create a naturalistic UK coastal community.
items.description: Polygonum paronychia is a species of flowering plant in the knotweed family known by the common names dune knotweed, black knotweed, and beach knotweed. It is native to the coastline of western North America from British Columbia to California, where it grows in sandy coastal habitat such as beaches, dunes, and scrub.

items.name: Polygonum polygaloides
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at two millimetres deep in early spring once the risk of hard frost has passed
Keep the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged to mimic its native damp gravelly habitat
Grow in full sun in poor sandy or gritty acidic soil to prevent the plant from becoming floppy
Watch for slugs and snails on young spring seedlings and protect them with organic wool pellets
Grow alongside moisture-loving dwarf rushes or sedges in a dedicated rock garden or gravel bed
items.description: Polygonum polygaloides is a North American species of flowering plants in the buckwheat family known by the common names milkwort knotweed and polygala knotweed. It is native to much of western North America, where it can be found in many types of moist habitat. It is a variable species, usually divided into a number of subspecies.

items.name: Polygonum ramosissimum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of 2mm in early spring using a gritty, free-draining seed compost.
Position in full sun and water sparingly once established to mimic dry, coastal UK shingle habitats.
Grow alongside low-growing coastal companion plants like Armeria maritima to prevent soil erosion.
Hand-weed surrounding soil early in spring to prevent faster-growing weeds from smothering seedlings.
Collect the small nutlet seeds in autumn before winter frosts cause the annual plant to die back.
items.description: Polygonum ramosissimum is a North American species of herbaceous annual plants in the buckwheat family, widespread across much of Canada and the United States, where it is commonly called bushy knotweed. It is susceptible to downy mildew caused by the oomycete species Peronospora americana.

items.name: Persicaria tinctoria
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds indoors in March at five millimetres deep to beat the short UK growing season.
Keep soil consistently damp like a wrung-out sponge; dry UK summers stunt leaf and dye yield.
Plant out in late May after frosts in rich soil mixed with plenty of well-rotted manure.
Harvest the top leaves in July before pink flowers appear to maximise the blue pigment content.
Protect young spring shoots from slugs and snails using organic beer traps or physical barriers.
items.description: Persicaria tinctoria is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family. Common names include Chinese indigo, Japanese indigo and dyer's knotweed. It is native to Southern China and Vietnam, and has been introduced to other parts of China, as well as Germany, Japan, Korea, Tibet, North and South Caucasus, parts of the Russian Far-East, and Ukraine.

items.name: Coccoloba diversifolia
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Caribbean shrub in a pot of loam-based compost to move indoors before autumn frosts.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil dries out to prevent root rot in cool UK weather.
Prune in late spring after new growth starts to maintain a compact shape and remove winter damage.
Keep in a conservatory or south-facing room from October to May to meet its high light requirements.
Check leaf undersides weekly for mealybugs and scale insects which thrive in dry indoor winter air.
items.description: Coccoloba diversifolia, known as pigeonplum or tietongue, is a species of the genus Coccoloba native to coastal areas of the Caribbean, Central America, southern Mexico, southern Florida and the Bahamas.

items.name: Bistorta officinalis
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive clay or boggy soil in partial shade to mimic UK damp meadow conditions.
Divide congested clumps in autumn or early spring using a sharp spade to maintain plant vigour.
Water deeply during dry UK summer spells to prevent the large leaves from wilting and browning.
Cut back faded flower spikes in July to encourage a second flush of pink blooms in late summer.
Position next to moisture-loving Astilbe or Iris pseudacorus for a contrasting foliage partnership.
items.description: Bistorta officinalis, known as bistort, common bistort, European bistort, or meadow bistort, is a species of flowering plant in the dock family Polygonaceae native to Europe and northern and western Asia. Other common names include snakeroot, snake-root, snakeweed, and Easter-ledges.

items.name: Devil's tail
items.growersTips:
Destroy this invasive weed immediately by pulling the shallow roots before it sets seeds in August.
Wear thick heavy-duty gloves to protect your hands from the sharp downward-pointing barbs on stems.
Bag all cleared vines and dispose of them in household waste rather than composting to stop spread.
Smother persistent seedbanks in damp soil with a thick double layer of black polythene silage wrap.
Check damp shaded areas near streams weekly from April for the distinctive triangular-shaped leaves.
items.description: Persicaria perfoliata is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family. Common names include mile-a-minute, devil's tail, giant climbing tearthumb, and Asiatic tearthumb. It is a trailing herbaceous annual vine with barbed stems and triangular leaves. It is native to most of temperate and tropical eastern Asia, occurring from eastern Russia and Japan in the north, and the range extending to the Philippines and India in the south.

items.name: Wood sorrel
items.growersTips:
Grow this mountain sorrel in gritty, acidic soil to mimic its native UK upland scree habitat.
Water consistently during dry summer spells to keep the soil damp but never waterlogged or stagnant.
Position in partial shade or a cool north-facing spot to prevent leaf scorch in southern UK heat.
Remove emerging flower spikes in summer to encourage a continuous flush of tender, edible leaves.
Sow seeds in autumn in cold frames to allow natural winter chilling for successful germination.
items.description: Oxyria is a genus of flowering plants in the family Polygonaceae with three accepted species. It has a circumboreal distribution in the northern hemisphere.

items.name: Persicaria virginiana
items.growersTips:
Plant in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade to prevent the variegated leaves from scorching.
Sow seeds shallowly in cold frames in autumn, as they require winter chill to germinate in the UK.
Divide established clumps in spring to control its vigorous spread and maintain plant vigour.
Watch for slugs and snails in damp UK springs, protecting the emerging young shoots with grit.
Cut back the flowered stems to the ground in late autumn to prevent excessive self-seeding.
items.description: Persicaria virginiana, also called jumpseed, Virginia knotweed or woodland knotweed is a North American species of smartweed within the buckwheat family. It is unusual as a shade-tolerant member of a mostly sun-loving genus. Jumpseed is a perennial, named for its seeds which can "jump" several feet when a ripe seedpod is disturbed.

items.name: Persicaria bistorta
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive clay or boggy soil in partial shade to prevent the foliage from drying out
Divide congested clumps in autumn or spring using a sharp spade to maintain vigor and propagate plants
Cut back faded flower spikes to the base in midsummer to encourage a second flush of pink blooms
Watch for vine weevil larvae in container-grown plants and treat with nematodes in late summer
Pair with Astilbe or Hostas in damp borders to create a contrasting foliage texture and color mix
items.description: Bistorta officinalis, known as bistort, common bistort, European bistort, or meadow bistort, is a species of flowering plant in the dock family Polygonaceae native to Europe and northern and western Asia. Other common names include snakeroot, snake-root, snakeweed, and Easter-ledges.

items.name: Bistorta vacciniifolia
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade to mimic alpine scree.
Water weekly during dry UK summers to keep the shallow, creeping root system from drying out.
Trim back dead flower spikes in late autumn to maintain a neat, carpet-like evergreen mat.
Propagate by dividing the rooting runners in spring just as new growth begins to emerge.
Position on a sloping rockery or raised bed to ensure excellent winter drainage in wet UK climates.
items.description: Bistorta vacciniifolia, the whortleberry-leaved knotweed, is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native to Tibet and the Himalaya. Well-suited for clay soils, as its synonym Persicaria vacciniifolia it has gained the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.

items.name: Calligonum leucocladum
items.growersTips:
Grow in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit to survive wet UK winters and prevent root rot.
Position in the brightest south-facing spot or greenhouse to mimic its native desert heat.
Water only when the soil is bone dry during summer and keep completely dry from October to March.
Prune back damaged stems in late spring after the last frost to encourage fresh needle-like growth.
Propagate by taking semi-ripe cuttings in midsummer using a very free-draining sandy compost mix.
items.description: Calligonum is a genus of plants in the family Polygonaceae with about 41 species native to Northern Africa, Western, South, and Central Asia, and central China.

items.name: Eriogonum caespitosum
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining grit-heavy soil to survive wet UK winters and prevent root rot.
Position in full south-facing sun against a warm wall to mimic its native dry habitat.
Water only during prolonged summer droughts, letting the soil dry out completely between times.
Protect the woolly foliage from winter wet using a temporary glass cloche or cold frame.
Propagate by taking semi-ripe cuttings in late summer rather than trying to divide the taproot.
items.description: Eriogonum caespitosum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name matted buckwheat, mat buckwheat, or cushion desert buckwheat.

items.name: Polygonum undulatum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at 2mm depth in April after the last frost using free-draining sandy loam soil.
Water seedlings twice weekly to keep soil damp but never waterlogged during dry UK summer spells.
Pinch out the growing tips in late May to encourage a bushier habit and prevent leggy stem growth.
Watch for dock beetles and shield bugs in June, removing them by hand to protect the soft foliage.
Plant alongside companion plants like Calendula to attract pollinators and mask the plant from pests.
items.description: Polygonum undulatum is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native to the Cape Provinces of South Africa. It was first described by Carl Linnaeus in 1753 as Atraphaxis undulata, and later transferred to Polygonum by Peter Jonas Bergius.

items.name: Fallopia dumetorum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring at 5mm depth in moist, well-drained soil once the risk of frost has passed.
Provide a sturdy trellis or pea netting early in May to support this vigorous climbing annual.
Water weekly at the base during dry summer spells to keep the soil consistently damp but not wet.
Watch for dock beetles and leaf miners in June, handpicking pests to protect the delicate foliage.
Clear and compost the entire plant in October before it drops seed to prevent unwanted spreading.
items.description: Fallopia dumetorum, also known as copse bindweed, is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native to temperate Eurasia.

items.name: Pteroxygonum giraldii
items.growersTips:
Plant the tuberous root five centimetres deep in late spring once the risk of UK frost has passed
Provide a sturdy trellis or obelisk to support its vigorous three-metre climbing habit by summer
Grow in moist but sharply draining soil amended with grit to prevent winter tuber rot in wet UK clay
Water deeply once a week during dry summer spells but keep the soil virtually dry throughout winter
Lift the tubers in late autumn and store in dry compost in a frost-free shed over the UK winter
items.description: Pteroxygonum giraldii is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, endemic to the Chinese provinces of Gansu, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Sichuan. It is found at altitudes of 600–2,000 m (2,000–6,600 ft). It grows to more than 3 m (10 ft) in height, with leaf blades triangular or triangular-ovate in shape, 4–7 cm (1.6–2.8 in) by 3–6 cm (1.2–2.4 in).

items.name: Bistorta officinalis
items.growersTips:
Plant Bistorta amplexicaulis in moisture-retentive clay soil in partial shade to prevent leaf scorch.
Divide congested clumps in early spring or autumn every three years to maintain vigorous flowering.
Cut back faded flower spikes of Bistorta affinis in midsummer to encourage a second flush of blooms.
Water deeply during dry UK summer spells to keep the soil consistently damp, especially in full sun.
Watch for slugs and snails on fresh spring shoots, protecting young growth with organic grit barriers.
items.description: Bistorta is a genus of flowering plants in the family Polygonaceae. As of February 2019 about 40 species are accepted. It has been supported as a separate clade by molecular phylogenetic analysis. Bistorta species are native throughout much of the Northern Hemisphere, as far south as Mexico in North America and Thailand in Asia.

items.name: Buckwheat
items.growersTips:
Sow perennial buckwheat seeds in late spring once UK frosts pass, at a shallow depth of one centimetre.
Grow in poor, well-drained soil to curb invasive spreading while encouraging better flower production.
Water young plants weekly during dry UK summers, but keep mature roots dry to prevent winter rot.
Cut the foliage back to ground level in late autumn to tidy the crown and prevent self-seeding.
Interplant with brassicas as a green manure to deter pests and accumulate calcium in UK plots.
items.description: The genus Fagopyrum is in the flowering plant family Polygonaceae. It includes some important food plants, such as F. esculentum (buckwheat) and F. tataricum. The genus is native to the Indian subcontinent, much of Indochina, central and southeastern China, and central and eastern tropical Africa. Species have been widely introduced elsewhere, throughout the Holarctic and parts of Africa and South America.

items.name: Persicaria minor
items.growersTips:
Plant this native moisture-lover in boggy soil or shallow pond margins up to ten centimetres deep.
Water daily during dry UK summers to keep the soil consistently saturated and prevent leaf scorch.
In autumn cut the faded stems back to the ground to keep the spreading clump tidy for spring growth.
Plant alongside Caltha palustris or Mentha aquatica to create a balanced British wetland display.
Watch for garden snails and slugs which target the tender young foliage during damp spring nights.
items.description: Persicaria minor is species of herb in the family Polygonaceae. Common names include pygmy smartweed, small water pepper and swamp willow weed. This herb is native to Asia, but distributed widely in Europe and Australia. It is used in South East Asian cooking.

items.name: Persicaria longiseta
items.growersTips:
Control this aggressive self-seeder by deadheading pink flower spikes in August before seeds drop.
Grow in a heavy clay or loam soil prepped with garden compost to retain the constant moisture it craves.
Plant in a damp, partially shaded border alongside moisture-loving hostas to suppress its spread.
Hand-pull shallow roots in spring when soil is wet to easily manage unwanted invasive clumps.
Water deeply twice a week during dry UK summers to prevent the lush green foliage from wilting.
items.description: Persicaria longiseta is a species of flowering plant in the knotweed family known by the common names Oriental lady's thumb, bristly lady's thumb, Asiatic smartweed, long-bristled smartweed, low smartweed, Asiatic waterpepper, bristled knotweed, bunchy knotweed, and tufted knotweed. It is native to Asia, and it is present in North America and Europe as an introduced species and often a weed.

items.name: Duma
items.growersTips:
Plant Duma florulenta in well-drained, gritty loam to prevent winter root rot in wet UK climates.
Water deeply once a week during dry summer spells, but let the soil dry out completely between waterings.
Prune back woody stems by one-third in early spring to encourage fresh, bushy growth and more flowers.
Protect young shoots from slugs and snails in damp British springs using organic beer traps or grit.
Propagate this perennial by taking semi-ripe cuttings in late summer to overwinter in a cold frame.
items.description: A duma is a Russian assembly with advisory or legislative functions.

items.name: Polygonum polymorphum
items.growersTips:
Plant in moist, fertile soil in spring, burying the root crown just level with the soil surface.
Water deeply once a week during dry UK summers to keep the soil consistently damp but not waterlogged.
Cut the hollow stems back to ground level in late autumn after the first frosts blacken the foliage.
Divide congested clumps in early spring using a sharp spade to maintain vigor and control the spread.
Position in full sun or partial shade, leaving two metres of space for its massive mature spread.
items.description: Koenigia alpina, commonly known as alpine knotweed, is similar to Koenigia alaskana, but differs in leaf size and achene characteristics. It is native to Europe and temperate Asia.

items.name: Bistorta affinis
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive clay or loam in full sun to partial shade, keeping the crown at soil level
Water weekly during dry UK summers to prevent the dense carpet of foliage from browning at the edges
Divide congested clumps in autumn or spring to rejuvenate growth and easily propagate new groundcover
Shear off faded brown flower spikes in late autumn to maintain a tidy mat and encourage fresh leaves
Pair with Astilbe or Hostas in damp borders where its low creeping habit suppresses weeds effectively
items.description: Bistorta affinis, the Himalayan bistort, fleece flower, or knotweed, is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native to the Himalayas.

items.name: Muehlenbeckia complexa
items.growersTips:
Plant in free-draining soil with grit to prevent winter root rot in wet UK climates.
Prune hard in early spring to control its vigorous, scrambling spread and maintain a neat shape.
Water newly planted shrubs weekly in summer, but leave established plants dry to encourage toughness.
Position in full sun or partial shade against a warm south-facing wall to protect from hard frosts.
Grow in a sturdy container to restrict its invasive root system and prevent it smothering neighbors.
items.description: Muehlenbeckia complexa is a plant commonly known as pohuehue, although this name also applies to some other climbers such as Muehlenbeckia australis.

items.name: Muehlenbeckia axillaris
items.growersTips:
Plant in free-draining gritty soil to prevent winter root rot in wet UK climates.
Prune hard in early spring to maintain a tight carpet and prevent the wiry stems from becoming bald.
Water sparingly once established, only during prolonged dry summer spells to avoid waterlogging.
Position in full sun to partial shade, ideally near a south-facing wall for protection from frost.
Propagate easily by detaching naturally layered stems that root where they touch the damp soil.
items.description: Muehlenbeckia axillaris is a low evergreen shrub, forming wiry mats up to about 1 metre in diameter, native to New Zealand, and the Australian states of Tasmania, New South Wales and Victoria. It has thin, red-brown stems, with glossy squarish to roundish leaves that are less than 1 cm (0.39 in) in diameter and 2–4 mm (0.079–0.157 in) thick. Flowers are inconspicuous, yellowish-white, 4–8 mm (0.16–0.31 in) in diameter, and borne in groups of up to three in the axils. The fruit is black, shiny, and up to 3.5 mm (0.14 in) long, produced in late summer to fall.

items.name: Fallopia japonica
items.growersTips:
Sow Fallopia convolvulus seeds directly outdoors in April once UK spring frosts have fully passed
Plant seeds at a shallow depth of five millimetres in well-drained soil with full sun exposure
Water young seedlings twice weekly during dry UK summer spells to establish strong climbing stems
Provide a sturdy trellis or obelisk immediately at planting to support the rapid twining habit
Check weekly for aphids and hand-wipe them off to prevent damage to the delicate heart-shaped leaves
items.description: Fallopia is a genus of about 12 species of flowering plants in the buckwheat family, in the past often included in a wider treatment of the related genus Polygonum, and previously including Reynoutria. The genus is native to temperate and subtropical regions of the Northern Hemisphere, but species have been introduced elsewhere. The genus includes species forming vines and shrubs.

items.name: Eriogonum angulosum
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining gritty soil or a raised scree bed to survive wet UK winter wetness.
Water sparingly only during prolonged summer droughts once established to prevent root rot.
Sow seeds shallowly in pots under cold frames during early spring to mimic natural cold stratification.
Protect young plants from slugs and snails during damp UK spring nights using physical barriers.
Grow alongside drought-tolerant companions like Sedums and Thymus in full south-facing sun.
items.description: Eriogonum angulosum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name anglestem buckwheat.

items.name: Eriogonum alpinum
items.growersTips:
Plant in a raised scree bed or alpine trough with fifty percent grit to survive wet UK winters.
Water only during prolonged summer droughts, keeping the foliage dry to prevent rot in humid air.
Protect the crown with a slate collar or gravel mulch to shed rain away from the plant base.
Prune back dead flower stems in late autumn to keep the compact mound tidy and prevent fungal damp.
Grow alongside slow-growing alpine sedums or sempervivums which share its extreme drainage needs.
items.description: Eriogonum alpinum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name Trinity buckwheat.

items.name: Eriogonum ampullaceum
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining grit-heavy soil to prevent winter root rot in wet UK climates.
Sow seeds shallowly in cold frames during autumn to mimic natural winter stratification.
Water sparingly only during prolonged summer droughts to avoid crown rot in damp UK weather.
Position in full south-facing sun against a brick wall to maximize essential summer heat.
Grow in raised beds or alpine troughs to ensure the perfect drainage this desert native needs.
items.description: Eriogonum ampullaceum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name Mono buckwheat.

items.name: Eriogonum apricum
items.growersTips:
Grow this rare dwarf buckwheat in a gritty alpine scree bed or container to ensure sharp drainage.
Protect from winter wet with a glass pane or cloche to prevent rot during damp UK winters.
Water sparingly only during dry summer spells once established to mimic its dry native habitat.
Plant in full sun in a mix of one part loam to three parts grit to replicate serpentine soils.
Propagate by taking softwood cuttings in early summer rather than relying on unreliable seed sets.
items.description: Eriogonum apricum is a rare species of wild buckwheat known by the common name Ione buckwheat. It is endemic to Amador County, California, in the United States.

items.name: Eriogonum arborescens
items.growersTips:
Plant this Channel Islands native in a raised bed or gravel garden with 50% grit to survive UK wet.
Water only during prolonged summer droughts once established, keeping the crown completely dry.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost risk passes to maintain its compact, mounded shape.
Protect from winter wet using a rain shelter or pot feet to prevent root rot in cold clay soils.
Propagate by taking semi-ripe heel cuttings in late summer to overwinter in a frost-free greenhouse.
items.description: Eriogonum arborescens is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name Santa Cruz Island buckwheat.

items.name: Bistorta amplexicaulis
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive clay or loam soil in partial shade to prevent midsummer leaf scorch.
Divide congested clumps in early spring or autumn to maintain vigour and propagate new plants.
Cut back faded flower spikes in late summer to encourage a second flush of blooms into autumn.
Water deeply during dry UK summer spells to stop the lower leaves from yellowing and dropping.
Combine with moisture-loving Astilbe or Deschampsia to create a classic British damp-border display.
items.description: Bistorta amplexicaulis, the red bistort or mountain fleece, is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family Polygonaceae, native to China, the Himalayas, and Pakistan. It is a damp-loving herbaceous perennial growing to 1.2 m (4 ft) tall and wide, with heart-shaped pointed leaves, downy beneath, and narrow spikes of rose-red or white flowers in summer.

items.name: Bistorta manshuriensis
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive clay or loam in partial shade to mimic cool UK woodland edge habitats.
Divide the vigorous root clumps every three years in early spring to control spread and renew vigor.
Mulch annually in March with well-rotted leafmould to maintain the high soil moisture it demands.
Water deeply during dry summer spells to prevent the large leaves from crisping and turning brown.
Position alongside moisture-loving UK companions like Astilbe or Hostas to mask post-flowering gaps.
items.description: Bistorta manshuriensis, Asian bistort, is an unresolved name for a proposed flowering plant species in the buckwheat family Polygonaceae. It is a perennial herbaceous plant found in mountain valleys and lowlands in Korea and Japan. It grows well in sunny or slightly shaded places. It grows up to 30 centimetres (12 in) - 80 centimetres (31 in).

items.name: Bistorta macrophylla
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive clay or loam in partial shade to mimic its native Himalayan habitat.
Water deeply during dry UK summer spells to prevent the large foliage from wilting and crisping.
Divide the dense rhizomatous root clumps in early spring to maintain vigor and control the spread.
Cut back the dead flower spikes and foliage to ground level in late autumn after the first frost.
Pair with Astilbe or Hostas in damp woodland borders to create a lush texture contrast.
items.description: Bistorta macrophylla is a flowering plant species in the buckwheat family Polygonaceae. It is native to mountain regions of West and South China, Bhutan, Nepal, northern India, and Pakistan.

items.name: Triplaris cumingiana
items.growersTips:
Grow this tropical plant in a heated greenhouse or conservatory to survive cold UK winters.
Plant in acidic to neutral loam mixed with grit and leaf mould to ensure excellent winter drainage.
Water copiously during the summer active growth phase but keep the soil barely damp throughout winter.
Prune in late winter before new growth starts to manage its vigorous height under glass ceilings.
Check regularly for glasshouse red spider mite and mealybugs under the leaves in dry summer heat.
items.description: Triplaris is a genus of plants in the family Polygonaceae. Ant tree is a common name for plants in this genus.

items.name: Fire bush
items.growersTips:
Grow this desert shrub in a terracotta pot using fifty percent grit to survive wet UK winters.
Place the pot in your hottest south facing suntrap or an unheated greenhouse to mimic desert heat.
Water only during active summer growth then keep the soil bone dry from October through to April.
Prune lightly in late spring only to remove winter dieback and maintain a compact branching shape.
Sow seeds in spring using a heated propagator set to twenty five degrees to trigger germination.
items.description: Calligonum comosum, the fire bush, arta or abal, is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae.

items.name: Eriogonum inflatum
items.growersTips:
Grow in a terracotta pot using a fifty-fifty mix of John Innes number two and coarse grit for drainage
Place the pot in the sunniest south-facing spot possible or under a rain shelter to mimic deserts
Water only when the soil is bone dry throughout spring and summer then keep completely dry in winter
Protect from winter wet and frost by moving the pot into a cold greenhouse or unheated conservatory
Prune away the dead inflated yellow stems in early spring before the new basal rosette growth starts
items.description: Eriogonum inflatum, the desert trumpet, is a perennial plant of the family Polygonaceae. The plant possesses very small yellow or pink flowers and an inflated stem just below branching segments. Eriogonum: from the Greek erion, "wool", and gonu, "joint or knee", in reference to the hairy or woolly joints of some of the species of the genus, but not particularly inflatum. It is found in the Mojave Desert and other deserts.

items.name: Eriogonum pyrolifolium
items.growersTips:
Plant in a raised scree bed or alpine trough with fifty percent grit to survive wet UK winters.
Water only during prolonged summer droughts, allowing the gritty soil to dry out completely between.
Protect the woolly foliage from winter wet using a glass or perspex pane held on wire pegs.
Propagate by taking semi-ripe heel cuttings in late summer and rooting them in sharp sand.
Grow alongside other drought-tolerant alpines like Sedum or Sempervivum in full, baking sun.
items.description: Eriogonum pyrolifolium is a species of wild buckwheat. It is native to western North America, from British Columbia to the high mountains of California.

items.name: Coccoloba caracasana
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender shrub in a pot of loam-based compost so you can move it indoors before UK frosts.
Water thoroughly once the top two inches of soil dry out, reducing this to a minimum in winter.
Prune in late spring after new growth starts to maintain its shape and remove frost-damaged stems.
Position in a conservatory or south-facing room to maximise light during dull UK autumn months.
Repot every two years in spring using a grit-heavy mix to ensure the sharp drainage it requires.
items.description: Coccoloba caracasana is a tree in the family Polygonaceae. It is known by the common name papaturro.

items.name: Persicaria dichotoma
items.growersTips:
Plant this moisture-lover in boggy soil or shallow pond margins up to ten centimetres deep.
Propagate by division in mid-spring to control its vigorous spread in small UK garden ponds.
Cut back the decaying foliage to the base in late autumn to keep the water clear and tidy.
In colder UK regions, mulch the crown heavily in November to protect it from hard winter frosts.
Pair with Caltha palustris to provide early spring colour before this foliage fully emerges.
items.description: Persicaria dichotoma is a species of flowering plant native to Australia and Asia.

items.name: Bistorta tenuicaulis
items.growersTips:
Plant in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade, mimicking UK woodland edges for best leaf growth.
Divide congested clumps in early spring just as new growth emerges to maintain plant vigour.
Keep soil consistently damp during dry UK summer spells to prevent the delicate foliage from wilting.
Protect the early spring emerging flower spikes from slugs and snails using organic beer traps.
Combine with shade-loving UK companions like hostas and ferns to cover its midsummer dormant phase.
items.description: Bistorta tenuicaulis is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native to South Korea and Japan. The species was first described as Polygonum tenuicaule by James Bisset and Spencer Moore in 1878, and transferred to the genus Bistorta by Takenoshin Nakai in 1926.

items.name: Fallopia convolvulus
items.growersTips:
Hand-pull young black-bindweed seedlings in May before their taproots anchor deeply in damp UK soil.
Hoe hoeable beds weekly in spring to sever the delicate stems of emerging seedlings at soil level.
Unwind the twining stems from your cultivated plants early in summer before they strangle growth.
Mulch borders with a five-centimetre layer of bark in March to suppress light-stimulated seeds.
Bag and dispose of mature plants in August before they drop hundreds of viable seeds into the soil.
items.description: Fallopia convolvulus, the black-bindweed or wild buckwheat, is a fast-growing annual flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae native throughout Europe, Asia and northern Africa.

items.name: Eriogonum umbellatum
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining grit-rich soil or raised gravel beds to survive wet UK winter wetness.
Water sparingly only during prolonged summer droughts once established to prevent crown rot.
Prune lightly in late spring by removing dead flower stems and tidying the evergreen foliage.
Position in full south-facing sun to mimic its native dry alpine meadow microclimate.
Grow alongside low-water Mediterranean herbs like thyme and dwarf lavenders in sunny borders.
items.description: Eriogonum umbellatum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name sulphurflower buckwheat, or simply sulphur flower.

items.name: Persicaria prostrata
items.growersTips:
Plant this creeping knotweed in moist, clay-heavy soil to mimic its native damp habitat.
Water deeply twice a week during dry UK summers to keep the prostrate foliage lush and green.
Position in full sun to partial shade to encourage the pink globe flowers from June to October.
Cut back the spreading stems hard in late autumn to control its vigorous, ground-covering habit.
Grow alongside moisture-loving Carex or hostas to create a dense, weed-suppressing ground cover.
items.description: Persicaria prostrata, basionym Polygonum prostratum, is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native to Australia and perhaps New Zealand. It is known by the common name of creeping knotweed.

items.name: Laksa Leaf
items.growersTips:
Grow in a pot to easily move this frost-tender herb indoors to a sunny windowsill before October.
Keep the soil constantly soggy by placing the pot in a shallow saucer filled with rainwater.
Plant in moisture-retentive, peat-free compost mixed with well-rotted manure for rich nutrients.
Harvest the young leaf tips weekly in summer to encourage bushy growth and prevent leggy stems.
Overwinter at temperatures above five degrees Celsius to prevent the tropical plant from dying.
items.description: Persicaria odorata is a species of flowering plant in the knotweed family, Polygonaceae. It is sometimes referred to by the common names Vietnamese coriander, rau răm, laksa leaf, Vietnamese cilantro, phak phai, praew leaf, hot mint, Cambodian mint and Vietnamese mint, is an herb whose leaves are used in Southeast Asian and Northeast Indian cooking.

items.name: Polygonum sawatchense
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in early spring once the frost risk has passed
Grow in poor sandy soil to restrict its spread and mimic its natural dry North American habitat
Water sparingly only during prolonged summer droughts as this annual thrives in dry gravelly beds
Watch for dock beetles in June and handpick them to prevent severe skeletonisation of the foliage
Plant alongside native UK fescues to provide structural support and prevent the weak stems lodging
items.description: Polygonum sawatchense is a North American species of plants in the buckwheat family. It in the western United States and western Canada, from the Pacific Coast to the western Great Plains, so from British Columbia south to California and east as far as New Mexico, Colorado, Saskatchewan, and the Dakotas.

items.name: Lesser red knotgrass
items.growersTips:
