Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in April once the UK spring soil begins to warm
Grow in poor sandy soil or gravelly scree beds to prevent this annual from becoming overly leggy
Water sparingly only during prolonged dry summer spells as this species is highly drought tolerant
Position in full south facing sun to ensure the plant completes its rapid annual life cycle
Clear dead plants in late autumn but leave some seed heads to allow natural self seeding for spring
items.description: Polygonum arenarium, the lesser red-knotgrass or European knotweed, is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae. It is native to Morocco, France, the former Czechoslovakia, Hungary, southeastern and eastern Europe, the Caucasus, Turkey, the Levant, Iraq, Iran, and Central Asia, and it has been introduced to Argentina, the British Isles, Germany, the Baltic States, and central European Russia. A scrambling or procumbent annual, it is often found in disturbed habitats. In more natural situations it is a psammophyte.

items.name: Polygonum bellardii
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in April once the spring soil begins to warm up.
Grow in poor to moderately fertile well-drained soil to prevent the plant from becoming too leggy.
Water sparingly once established as this annual is highly drought-tolerant in dry UK summers.
Position in full sun to ensure robust stem development and to maximise its delicate pink flowering.
Clear dead plants in late autumn to prevent excessive self-seeding across your borders next spring.
items.description: Polygonum bellardii, the narrowleaf knotweed, is a species of annual herb in the family Polygonaceae. They have a self-supporting growth form and simple, broad leaves. They are native to Southern Europe, West Asia and North Africa. Individuals can grow to 0.49 m.

items.name: Polygonum achoreum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in early spring once UK frosts have fully passed
Keep soil consistently moist but never waterlogged during the initial six weeks of seedling growth
Watch for dock beetles and leaf beetles which skeletonise the foliage of this polygonaceae species
Grow alongside companion plants like chamomile or thyme to help suppress surrounding aggressive weeds
Incorporate grit into heavy UK clay soils to ensure the sharp drainage this annual species requires
items.description: Polygonum achoreum, common names Blake's knotweed, leathery knotweed or striate knotweed, is a North American species of plants in the buckwheat family. It is widespread across much of Canada and the northern United States.

items.name: Polygonum tenue
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in early spring once the last UK frost has passed
Grow in poor sandy or gravelly soil with sharp drainage to mimic its native dry pavement habitat
Water sparingly only during prolonged summer droughts as this annual is highly drought tolerant
Position in full south facing sun to ensure the plant completes its life cycle and sets seed
Allow the plant to self seed naturally in autumn to guarantee its return in the same spot next year
items.description: Polygonum tenue, the slender knotweed or pleat-leaf knotweed, is a North American species of plant in the buckwheat family. It is widespread across south-central Canada (Ontario) and the eastern and central United States from Maine to Georgia, west as far as Minnesota, South Dakota, Nebraska, and Texas.

items.name: Eriogonum fasciculatum
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining grit-heavy soil on a south-facing slope to survive wet UK winters.
Water only during severe summer droughts once established to prevent root rot in damp climates.
Prune lightly in late spring after frosts pass to shape the shrub and remove winter dieback.
Grow in a raised bed or terracotta pot to keep the roots dry during persistent autumn rains.
Position near rosemary or lavender in full sun to match Mediterranean-style growing conditions.
items.description: Eriogonum fasciculatum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common names California buckwheat and flat-topped buckwheat. Characterized by small, white and pink flower clusters that give off a cottony effect, this species grows variably from a patchy mat to a wide shrub, with the flowers turning a rusty color after blooming. This plant is of great benefit across its various habitats, providing an important food resource for a diversity of insect and mammal species. It also provides numerous ecosystem services for humans, including erosion control, post-fire mitigation, increases in crop

items.name: Polygonum majus
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring at a depth of 5mm directly into moist, well-drained soil after the last frost.
Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged, watering at the base weekly during dry UK summers.
Position in full sun to partial shade, preparing the bed with garden compost to mimic woodland edges.
Watch for slugs and snails on young spring shoots, using beer traps or organic wool pellets to deter.
Grow alongside companion plants like Persicaria or native grasses to support its sprawling habit.
items.description: Polygonum majus is a North American species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name wiry knotweed. It grows in the western United States and western Canada, from British Columbia south as far as the Sierra Nevada of northwestern Inyo County in California, east as far as Montana.

items.name: Persicaria mitis
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive clay or loam near pond edges to mimic its native UK wetland habitat.
Sow seeds in autumn at a depth of 5mm to allow natural winter chilling to break seed dormancy.
Water weekly during dry summer spells to keep the soil consistently damp, mimicking bog conditions.
Cut back dead stems to ground level in late autumn to prevent self-seeding and tidy the winter plot.
Plant alongside Marsh Marigold or Water Forget-me-not to create a cohesive native UK wetland display.
items.description: Persicaria mitis (Schrank) Assenov is a species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native to Europe.

items.name: Western bistort
items.growersTips:
Plant in moisture-retentive clay or loamy soil in a bog garden or beside a pond in partial shade.
Sow seeds in cold frames during autumn to allow the natural winter chill to break their dormancy.
Divide mature clumps in early spring or autumn to control spread and maintain vigorous flowering.
Water deeply during dry UK summer spells to keep the soil consistently damp and prevent leaf scorch.
Plant alongside Astilbe or moisture-loving Iris pseudacorus to create a natural pond-edge display.
items.description: Bistorta bistortoides, commonly called western bistort, is a perennial herb in the buckwheat family. It grows mainly in the western United States, but also extends into small areas of southern Canada and northern Mexico. It is an edible plant that is part of the traditional diet of native peoples.

items.name: Coccoloba pubescens
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Caribbean native in a pot of loam-based compost so you can move it indoors by October
Water thoroughly only when the top three inches of soil dry out to prevent root rot in cool weather
Wipe the massive leaves weekly with a damp cloth to prevent red spider mite infestations indoors
Prune in late spring just as new growth starts to control its size for indoor winter housing
Keep winter temperatures strictly above twelve degrees Celsius to prevent leaf drop and dieback
items.description: Coccoloba pubescens, known as grandleaf seagrape, largeleaf, mountain-grape, and Eve's umbrella, is a species of Coccoloba native to coastal regions of the Caribbean: on Antigua, Barbados, Barbuda, Dominica, Hispaniola, Martinique, Montserrat, and Puerto Rico.

items.name: Bistorta vivipara
items.growersTips:
Plant bulbils 1cm deep in autumn in moist, organic-rich soil to mimic UK upland meadow conditions.
Water frequently to keep the soil consistently damp, especially during dry southern UK summers.
Grow alongside Primula denticulata or Trollius europaeus which thrive in the same damp, cool soils.
Remove fading flower spikes in late summer to prevent unwanted self-seeding from fallen bulbils.
Watch for slugs and snails in spring as they target the tender emerging red-tinged foliage.
items.description: Bistorta vivipara is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the knotweed and buckwheat family Polygonaceae, commonly known as alpine bistort. Scientific synonyms include Bistorta vivipara and Polygonum viviparum. It is common all over the high Arctic through Europe, North America, incl. Greenland, and temperate and tropical Asia. Its range stretches further south in high mountainous areas such as the Alps, Carpathians, Pyrenees, Caucasus, Alaska and the Tibetan Plateau.

items.name: Coccoloba uvifera
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender shrub in a pot of loam-based compost so you can move it indoors before first frost.
Water deeply once the top two inches of soil dry out, reducing this to once a month during winter.
Prune in late spring to control size, cutting just above a leaf node to encourage bushier growth.
Position in your brightest south-facing room or heated conservatory to meet its high light needs.
Feed fortnightly from April to September using a balanced liquid fertiliser diluted to half strength.
items.description: Coccoloba uvifera is a species of tree and flowering plant in the buckwheat family, Polygonaceae. Its common names include seagrape and baygrape. It is native to coastal beaches throughout tropical America and the Caribbean. It has edible fruit, among other uses.

items.name: Persicaria wallichii
items.growersTips:
Grow this highly invasive plant only in a large, sturdy container to prevent spread via rhizomes.
Submerge the pot in a bog garden or keep soil constantly wet to mimic its native damp habitat.
Cut stems to the ground in late autumn and bag the debris to prevent self-seeding in your garden.
Plant in partial shade to protect the foliage from scorching during hot UK summer afternoons.
Wear gloves when handling to avoid skin irritation from the sap when cutting back the hollow stems.
items.description: Koenigia polystachya is a species of flowering plant in the knotweed family, known by the common names Himalayan knotweed and cultivated knotweed. It has several regularly used synonyms, including Polygonum polystachyum, Aconogonon polystachyum and Persicaria wallichii.

items.name: Brunnichia
items.growersTips:
Plant in a sheltered south-facing spot using deep gritty loam to mimic its native riverbank habitat
Provide a sturdy trellis or pergola to support its vigorous woody tendrils as it climbs in summer
Water deeply once a week during dry summer spells but keep soil relatively dry throughout winter
Prune hard in late winter to restrict spread and encourage fresh flowering wood for the summer
Mulch the root zone heavily with straw in November to protect the crown from severe UK frosts
items.description: Brunnichia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Polygonaceae. It includes a single species, Brunnichia ovata, commonly known as redvine, American buckwheat vine or ladies' eardrops, a woody vine native to the central and southeastern United States.

items.name: Dodecahema
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring at a depth of 3mm in a gritty, free-draining loam to prevent winter wet rot.
Position in full sun next to low-growing Sedums to mimic its natural dry, open habitat.
Water sparingly only when the top 5cm of soil is dry, as this annual dislikes UK dampness.
Protect young seedlings from slugs using organic grit barriers during wet British spring nights.
Collect seeds in late summer before autumn rains rot the seed heads to ensure next year's crop.
items.description: Dodecahema is a genus of plants in the family Polygonaceae with a single species restricted to California, where it is an endangered species on the state and federal levels. Its common name is slender-horned spineflower. This is a small annual plant forming a patch of spreading basal leaves a few centimeters in diameter, or slightly larger when more moisture is available. It bolts an erect stalk upon which it bears inflorescences of flowers. Each group of white or pink flowers is enclosed in a tiny cup of fused bracts which is only a few millimeters wide. The fruit is a dark achene about 2 mil

items.name: Rheum ribes
items.growersTips:
Plant in deep, fertile, free-draining soil with a pH of 6.0 to 6.8 to mimic its native rocky slopes.
Sow seeds indoors in early spring at a depth of 1.5cm, keeping temperatures around 15 to 20 Celsius.
Water deeply once a week during dry UK summers, keeping the crown dry to prevent rot in damp weather.
Protect young spring shoots from slugs and snails using organic grit barriers or beer traps.
Do not harvest any stalks in the first two years to allow the deep taproot system to establish.
items.description: Rheum ribes, the Syrian rhubarb or currant-fruited rhubarb, or warty-leaved rhubarb, is an edible wild rhubarb species in the genus Rheum. It grows between 1000 and 4000 m on dunite rocks, among stones and slopes, and is now distributed in the temperate and subtropical regions of the world, chiefly in Western Asia to Afghanistan and Pakistan and also in ladakh(Kargil) region of India. The Syrian rhubarb is a partially commercial vegetable collected from wild patches in Eastern and Southern Anatolia, Kurdistan, and partly Northwestern Iran in early spring. Rheum ribes is considered as a valuabl

items.name: Chorizanthe
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of two millimetres in early spring using a cold frame to protect them.
Grow in a sharply draining, gritty soil mix with added perlite to survive wet UK spring weather.
Water sparingly only when the top five centimetres of soil are dry to prevent root rot in damp air.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot of your garden to mimic their native arid environment.
Plant alongside drought-tolerant sedums or sempervivums to create a compatible dry gravel garden.
items.description: Chorizanthe is a genus of plants in the buckwheat family known generally as spineflowers. These are small, squat, herbaceous plants with spiny-looking inflorescences of flowers. The flowers may be in shades of red or yellow to white. The bracts are pointed and sometimes tipped with a hooked awn, and the inflorescence often dries into a rounded, spiny husk. Spineflowers are found in western North America and South America.

items.name: Fagopyrum esculentum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in late spring after the last frost at a depth of two centimetres in well-drained soil.
Water young seedlings weekly during dry spells but avoid waterlogging to prevent root rot.
Watch for slugs and snails on tender young shoots during damp UK spring nights and use barriers.
Incorporate organic matter into poor sandy soils before sowing to help retain essential moisture.
Grow alongside brassicas as a green manure to suppress weeds and attract beneficial pollinators.
items.description: Buckwheat or common buckwheat is a flowering plant in the knotweed family Polygonaceae cultivated for its grain-like seeds and as a cover crop. Buckwheat cultivation originated around the 6th millennium BC in the region of what is now Yunnan Province in southwestern China. The name "buckwheat" is used for several other species, such as Fagopyrum tataricum, a domesticated food plant raised in Asia.

items.name: Antigonon
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Mexican vine in a large pot so you can move it into a heated greenhouse for winter.
Plant in free-draining gritty loam to prevent root rot during wet British autumns and winters.
Prune stems back to the base in late winter to encourage vigorous new flowering growth in spring.
Water sparingly in winter but keep soil damp during summer to support the intense pink blooms.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot or conservatory to meet its high heat and light needs.
items.description: Antigonon is a genus of flowering plants in the buckwheat family, Polygonaceae. It contains three species native to the Americas.

items.name: Eriogonum jamesii
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining grit-heavy soil to prevent root rot during wet UK winters.
Position in full south-facing sun to mimic its native dry American southwest habitat.
Water only during prolonged summer droughts once established to avoid overwatering.
Protect the crown from winter wet using a rain shelter or a deep layer of gravel mulch.
Grow alongside other drought-tolerant rock garden plants like sedums and sempervivums.
items.description: Eriogonum jamesii is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name James' buckwheat and antelope sage. It is native to the southwestern United States, being found in: Colorado, Utah, Arizona, Texas, New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Nebraska.

items.name: Aconogonon
items.growersTips:
Plant Aconogonon campanulatum in moisture-retentive, humus-rich soil that does not dry out in summer.
Divide mature clumps in early spring just as new growth emerges to control its vigorous spread.
Cut the hollow stems back to ground level in late autumn after the first frosts blacken the foliage.
Grow in partial shade to mimic UK woodland edges, preventing leaf scorch during dry summer spells.
Combine with moisture-loving Astilbe or Hostas to mask the bare lower stems of taller varieties.
items.description: Koenigia is a genus of plants in the family Polygonaceae. The genus Aconogonon has been merged into Koenigia.

items.name: Eriogonum argophyllum
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining gritty scree or alpine gravel to survive wet UK winters without rotting.
Grow in a terracotta pot with grit-heavy compost so you can move it under a cold frame during rain.
Water only during prolonged dry summer spells once established, keeping the crown completely dry.
Position in your garden's absolute fullest south-facing sun to mimic its native Great Basin light.
Surround the base with a thick layer of granite grit rather than organic mulch to prevent rot.
items.description: Eriogonum argophyllum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common names Sulphur Hot Springs buckwheat, Silver Lake buckwheat, and Ruby Valley buckwheat. It is endemic to Nevada in the United States, where there is only one known population.

items.name: Eriogonum brachypodum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in early spring under glass using a gritty, free-draining compost to prevent dampening off.
Plant out in late May in the sunniest spot available, ensuring the soil is poor, sandy, and dry.
Water sparingly only during prolonged dry spells, as this desert annual easily rots in UK wet.
Protect young plants from slugs and snails which target the tender early growth in damp UK springs.
Grow alongside other drought-tolerant gravel garden plants like Sedums to mimic its natural habitat.
items.description: Eriogonum brachypodum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name Parry's buckwheat. This annual herb is native to the southwestern United States from California to Utah and especially the Mojave Desert. It grows in sandy and gravelly substrates. It has a skeletonlike spindly stem which branches many times. It can grow 5 to 50 centimeters in height and up to a meter in width. There is an array of rounded, dark-colored leaves around the base. Leaves are a few centimeters long and fuzzy on the undersides. Most of the plant is actually the spreading inflorescence. At intervals on the

items.name: Eriogonum baileyi
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in early spring under glass using a gritty, free-draining compost to prevent damp-off.
Plant out in late May in your sunniest, south-facing gravel garden or alpine scree bed.
Water sparingly only during prolonged dry spells, as this desert annual rots easily in UK rain.
Position near low-growing sedums or sempervivums which share its need for sharply drained soil.
Collect the papery seed heads in autumn to sow next year, as it will not reliably self-seed in wet.
items.description: Eriogonum baileyi is a species of wild buckwheat that is commonly known as Bailey's buckwheat. It is native to the western United States, where it is a common member of the flora in several types of sandy habitat, such as desert and sagebrush. Eriogonum baileyi is an annual herb. It produces a spreading to erect, often wool-coated stem up to about half a meter tall. Leaves are woolly, round and located at the base of the plant. The inflorescence is a branching cyme bearing many clusters of flowers. The individual flowers are 1 to 2 millimeters wide and white or pink in color.

items.name: Eriogonum brachyanthum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in early spring under glass in a gritty, free-draining compost to prevent winter rot.
Plant out in late May in the poorest, sharp-draining soil or gravel to mimic its desert habitat.
Water sparingly only during prolonged dry spells, allowing the soil to dry out completely.
Position in the absolute maximum full sun available, such as a south-facing gravel bed or rockery.
Protect young seedlings from slugs and snails using physical barriers during damp UK spring nights.
items.description: Eriogonum brachyanthum is a species of wild buckwheat that is commonly known as shortflower buckwheat. It is native to eastern California and western Nevada, particularly the Mojave Desert region, where it is common to abundant, and even sometimes weedy. It is also known from southern Oregon. The plant grows in sandy habitats such as desert flats and sagebrush. It also grows in pinyon-juniper and montane conifer woodlands. It is an annual herb that grows 30 to 40 centimeters tall. Leaves are located at the base of the stem, woolly, and oval or rounded in shape. The top of the stem is occupied

items.name: Eriogonum callistum
items.growersTips:
Plant this alpine buckwheat in a raised bed or scree garden with fifty percent grit for wet winters.
Water only during prolonged summer droughts, allowing the gritty soil to dry out completely between.
Protect the crown from winter wet by applying a thick collar of granite or quartzite gravel mulch.
Grow alongside Thymus serpyllum or Sedum album to mimic its natural dry, rocky mountain habitat.
Propagate by taking semi-ripe heel cuttings in late summer and rooting them in a cold frame.
items.description: Eriogonum callistum is a rare species of wild buckwheat, known by the common name Tehachapi buckwheat.

items.name: Eriogonum butterworthianum
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining grit-heavy soil on a south-facing slope to survive wet UK winters.
Water only during prolonged summer droughts once established to prevent root rot in damp UK clay.
Prune lightly in late spring after frosts pass to maintain its compact, mounded shrub habit.
Protect from winter wet using a rain shelter or grow in an alpine house to prevent crown rot.
Grow alongside Thymus or Sedum in a gravel bed to match its strict low-nutrient soil needs.
items.description: Eriogonum butterworthianum is a rare species of wild buckwheat known by the common name Butterworth's buckwheat. It is endemic to the Santa Lucia Mountains of central Monterey County, California, where it is known from a few occurrences in the wilderness southeast of Big Sur in the vicinity of Junipero Serra Peak. Its native habitats include oak and conifer woodlands, chaparral communities, and sandstone outcrops. Eriogonum butterworthianum is a small clumpy shrub or subshrub that grows up to about 30 centimeters tall and wide. Leaves are 2 centimeters long and reddish-green in color. They are

items.name: Eriogonum cithariforme
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining gritty soil or scree to prevent winter wet rot in damp UK climates.
Position in full south-facing sun against a warm wall to mimic its native arid habitat.
Water sparingly only during prolonged summer droughts, keeping the crown completely dry in winter.
Protect from slugs and snails in spring when tender new growth emerges in damp British weather.
Prune back spent flower stems in late autumn to keep the mounded perennial habit neat and compact.
items.description: Eriogonum cithariforme is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name cithara buckwheat.

items.name: Eriogonum cernuum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring on the surface of gritty, free-draining compost as they need light to germinate.
Grow in terracotta pots with 50% grit to protect the roots from wet winter rot in damp UK climates.
Water only when the top three inches of soil are dry, mimicking its native arid North American home.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot of your garden to maximize summer heat and flower yield.
Sow alongside gravel-loving annuals like Eschscholzia californica to fill gaps in dry rock gardens.
items.description: Eriogonum cernuum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name nodding buckwheat. It is native to much of western North America, where it grows in sandy and gravelly habitat, including woodland and sagebrush. It is an annual herb growing up to about 60 centimeters in maximum height with a thin, branching flowering stem. The rounded, woolly leaves are one or two centimeters wide and are mainly located about the base of the stem. The inflorescence is evenly lined with hanging involucres of flowers. The individual flowers are less than 2 millimeters wide and white to pink-tinged in col

items.name: Eriogonum cinereum
items.growersTips:
Plant in gritty free-draining soil mixed with horticultural grit to prevent winter root rot in UK rain.
Position in the absolute sunniest south-facing spot or against a warm wall to mimic coastal California.
Water sparingly only during dry summer spells and keep completely dry during wet British winters.
Prune lightly in late spring after frosts pass to shape the shrub and remove winter-damaged stems.
Grow in a raised bed or terracotta pot to ensure the rapid drainage this drought-tolerant plant needs.
items.description: Eriogonum cinereum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common names coastal buckwheat and ashyleaf buckwheat.

items.name: Eriogonum contiguum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly in early spring using a gritty, free-draining compost mix under a cold frame.
Position in the sunniest spot possible, using raised beds or gravel scree to mimic desert drainage.
Water sparingly only during dry spells, allowing the soil to dry out completely between waterings.
Protect young plants from slugs and snails using physical barriers during damp UK spring nights.
Grow alongside other drought-tolerant alpine plants like Sedums to create a compatible microclimate.
items.description: Eriogonum contiguum is an uncommon species of wild buckwheat. It is commonly known as Reveal's buckwheat and annual desert trumpet. It is native to Death Valley in California and adjacent sections of Nevada. It is commonly found in Death Valley National Park and Mojave National Preserve. Eriogonum contiguum grows in sandy to gravelly flats and slopes, or rocky hills, and lower bajadas with Atriplex species. It is an annual herb which produces an erect, spreading stem up to about 30 centimeters high. Leaves are basal, small rounded, and woolly. The many scattered inflorescences are small, compa

items.name: Eriogonum congdonii
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining grit-heavy soil to prevent root rot during wet UK winters.
Position in full sun against a south-facing wall to mimic its native warm Californian climate.
Water sparingly only during prolonged summer droughts once the shrub is fully established.
Prune lightly in late spring after frosts pass to maintain a compact dome shape and remove deadwood.
Protect young plants from slugs and snails during damp UK springs using physical barriers or grit.
items.description: Eriogonum congdonii is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name Congdon's buckwheat. It is endemic to the Klamath Mountains of northern California, where it is an uncommon member of the serpentine soils flora in the local forests. It is a low, matting shrub growing up to about half a meter wide and tall. The woolly leaves are widely lance-shaped and are found along the stems, especially in clusters at the stem tips. The inflorescence is an erect, dense umbel of many tiny bright yellow flowers.

items.name: Eriogonum crocatum
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining gritty soil or a raised scree bed to survive wet UK winters.
Position in full south-facing sun against a warm house wall to mimic its native Californian heat.
Water only during prolonged dry summer spells and keep completely dry during damp winter months.
Protect the woolly silver foliage from winter wet using a glass cloche or open-sided cold frame.
Prune lightly in late spring by pinching back tips to maintain a compact mounded growth habit.
items.description: Eriogonum crocatum, the Conejo buckwheat or saffron buckwheat, is a species of Eriogonum, or wild buckwheat. It is endemic to the Conejo Valley and surrounding regions in Ventura County, California. It grows on open, dry hillsides, often in crags in rock faces.

items.name: Eriogonum deflexum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in early spring under glass in a gritty, free-draining compost mix at a depth of two millimetres.
Grow in terracotta pots using a mix of half John Innes number one and half horticultural grit.
Water only when the potting mix is bone dry, keeping the foliage dry to prevent winter damp rot.
Position in the sunniest, most sheltered spot of the garden to mimic its native desert heat.
Sow alongside Eschscholzia californica in a gravel bed to create a drought-tolerant display.
items.description: Eriogonum deflexum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common names flatcrown buckwheat, flat-top buckwheat, and skeletonweed. This plant is native to the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico, where it is common and grows in a variety of habitats, especially desert scrub. It is somewhat weedy where it is most abundant. This is an annual which varies in size from small patches on the ground to tangled bushes approaching two meters in height; it may be dense or thin and spindly. This is a brown or greenish weedy-looking herb with a many-branched stem. The leaves are located

items.name: Eriogonum davidsonii
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in early spring on the surface of gritty, free-draining compost as they need light to sprout
Grow in terracotta pots with alpine grit to protect the roots from wet winter rot in UK dampness
Place in the sunniest south-facing spot of the garden to mimic its native dry Californian climate
Water sparingly only during prolonged dry summer spells, allowing the soil to dry out completely
Plant alongside hardy sedums and sempervivums which share its extreme drought and low-nutrient needs
items.description: Eriogonum davidsonii is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name Davidson's buckwheat. This plant is native to the southwestern United States and northern Baja California. It grows in sandy or gravelly soils, mixed grassland, saltbush, chaparral, sagebrush communities as well as oak and montane conifer woodland. It is a spindly annual herb growing up to 40 centimeters in height. Leaves are fuzzy, basal, and round with wavy or wrinkly margins fuzzy. They are two centimeters wide. The plant is variable in appearance, but is usually erect with thin, naked, neatly branching stems beari

items.name: Eriogonum douglasii
items.growersTips:
Plant in extremely sharp-draining grit-heavy soil to survive wet UK winters and prevent root rot.
Position in full south-facing sun to mimic its native dry habitat and encourage summer flowering.
Water only during prolonged dry spells in summer and keep completely dry during damp winter months.
Grow in a raised alpine bed or terracotta pot so you can easily move it under a winter rain shelter.
Surround the plant base with a thick layer of granite grit to protect the foliage from wet soil.
items.description: Eriogonum douglasii is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name Douglas' buckwheat. It is native to the western United States, including the Pacific Northwest and part of the Great Basin.

items.name: Eriogonum elatum
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining gritty soil or a raised gravel bed to survive wet UK winter root rot.
Position in full south-facing sun against a warm wall to mimic its native arid US habitat.
Water sparingly only during dry summer spells once established to prevent crown rot in UK damp.
Protect the crown with a slate pane or cloche during persistent British winter rain and snow.
Propagate by sowing seeds in cold frames during autumn to allow natural winter stratification.
items.description: Eriogonum elatum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name tall woolly buckwheat. It is native to the western United States from California to Idaho. It is a perennial herb varying in size from one half to 1.5 meters in height. Its long leaves are located at the base of the plant and can be quite long for a buckwheat, over 20 centimeters in maximum length. The erect, branching stems are thin and naked and occasionally hollow. The plant produces small to large inflorescences with clusters of tiny flowers in shades of white to dark pink.

items.name: Eriogonum diclinum
items.growersTips:
Plant this dioecious Oregon buckwheat in sharply draining grit-heavy soil to survive wet UK winters.
Position in full south-facing sun against a warm brick wall to mimic its native dry mountain slopes.
Water sparingly only during prolonged summer droughts once established to prevent fatal root rot.
Prune lightly in late spring after frosts pass to shape the shrub and remove winter-damaged stems.
Protect from winter wet using a rain shelter or cloche if your UK garden has heavy clay soil.
items.description: Eriogonum diclinum is a species of wild buckwheat known by the common name Jaynes Canyon buckwheat. It is native to the Klamath Mountains of northern California and southern Oregon, where it is an uncommon member of plant communities on serpentine soils. This is a small dioecious shrub forming low, thick mats rarely exceeding 20 centimeters in height. The curving, oval-shaped leaves are woolly and greenish gray in color, growing up to two centimeters long. The plant flowers in yellow to reddish rounded inflorescences, male plants producing clusters of staminate flowers, and female plants produ

items.name: Eriogonum exilifolium
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining grit-heavy soil to survive wet UK winters and prevent fatal root rot.
Position in full south-facing sun to mimic its native dry habitat and prevent leggy growth.
Water only during prolonged summer droughts, keeping the crown completely dry during winter.
Protect from winter wet using a rain shelter or cloche from November through to March.
Grow in a raised scree bed or alpine trough to ensure the rapid drainage this perennial requires.
items.description: Eriogonum exilifolium is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family known by the common name dropleaf buckwheat. It is native to Wyoming and Colorado in the United States.

items.name: Eriogonum flavum
items.growersTips:
Plant in sharply draining grit-heavy soil to prevent winter wet rot in damp UK climates.
Position in full south-facing sun against a warm wall to mimic its native dry alpine habitat.
Water only during prolonged summer droughts once established as this plant is highly drought-tolerant.
Protect the crown with a slate collar or gravel mulch to keep wet winter soil off the foliage.
Propagate by taking semi-ripe heel cuttings in late summer rather than relying on unreliable UK seed.
items.description: Eriogonum flavum is a species of wild buckwheat.

items.name: Salicornia europaea
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly in spring on a moist, free-draining sandy compost mix mimicking UK saltmarshes.
Water weekly with salt water using one teaspoon of non-iodized sea salt per litre of tap water.
Grow in full sun in a cold frame or greenhouse to protect young seedlings from late UK frosts.
Harvest by snipping the tender green tips in midsummer before the stems turn woody and red in autumn.
Avoid waterlogging by using free-draining pots with gravel bases rather than heavy garden clay.
items.description: Salicornia europaea, known as marsh samphire, common glasswort or just glasswort, is a halophytic annual dicot flowering plant. Other common names include pickle weed, saltwort, and chicken toe. It is a succulent plant with high water content, accounting for its slightly translucent look. It is found near saline water in Europe and is edible both raw and cooked.

items.name: Maireana sedifolia
items.growersTips:
Grow in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit to survive wet winters and move indoors by November
Water only when the soil is bone dry from May to September and keep completely dry during winter
Prune lightly in late spring after frost to shape the shrub but never cut back into old woody stems
Position in the hottest south facing spot to maximise intense summer sun and prevent foliage rotting
Plant alongside hardy sedums or sempervivums in a raised gravel bed to ensure rapid water drainage
items.description: Maireana sedifolia, also known as pearl bluebush, pearl saltbush, hoary bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to arid parts of inland Australia. It is a compact, widely branching shrub with fleshy, narrowly egg-shaped leaves, pairs of densely woolly bisexual flowers, and a firm, thin-walled fruiting perianth with a papery, horizontal wing.

items.name: Maireana aphylla
items.growersTips:
Grow in free-draining gritty soil with added perlite to prevent root rot during wet UK winters.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot or a greenhouse to mimic its native Australian heat.
Water only when the soil is bone dry, reducing to zero watering from November through February.
Prune lightly in late spring after frosts pass to maintain its compact, tangled shrub shape.
Overwinter in a pot to easily move indoors before autumn frosts dip below minus five Celsius.
items.description: Maireana aphylla, commonly known as cotton bush or leafless bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a widely branched, mostly dioecious shrub with small, woolly leaves, flowers arranged singly, and a fruiting perianth with a small tube and horizontal wings.

items.name: Maireana georgei
items.growersTips:
Grow this Australian desert native in a pot with fifty percent grit to survive wet UK winters.
Bring your potted plant indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or sunny windowsill from October to April.
Water only when the soil is completely dry, reducing to once a month during the cold winter months.
Prune lightly in late spring after the last frost to maintain a compact shape and prevent legginess.
Position in your garden's hottest, most south-facing spot to maximise essential summer sun exposure.
items.description: Maireana georgei, commonly known as slit-wing bluebush or satiny bluebush, is a flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a grey-green perennial shrub with woolly branches and small flowers.

items.name: Salicornia bigelovii
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds in spring at 5mm depth in a free-draining sandy compost mix kept constantly moist.
Water daily with a 1 percent sea salt solution to mimic coastal marshes and prevent bitter stems.
Grow in a greenhouse or sunny south-facing cold frame to provide the high heat this annual needs.
Harvest by pinching out the tender top 5cm of shoots in midsummer to encourage a bushier habit.
Position next to sea kale or sea aster in containers to manage their shared high-salinity needs.
items.description: Salicornia bigelovii is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae known by the common names dwarf saltwort and dwarf glasswort. It is native to coastal areas of the eastern and southern United States, Belize, and coastal Mexico. It is a plant of salt marshes, a halophyte which grows in saltwater. It is an annual herb producing an erect, branching stem which is jointed at many internodes. The fleshy, green to red stem can reach about 60 cm in height. The leaves are usually small plates, pairs of which are fused into a band around the stem. The inflorescence is a dense, sticklike

items.name: Tecticornia arbuscula
items.growersTips:
Grow in a free-draining saline soil mix of coarse sand and grit to mimic native saltmarsh habitats.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot possible or under unheated glass to survive UK dampness.
Water sparingly only when the potting medium dries out completely to prevent root rot in winter.
Protect from frost below minus five Celsius by moving containers into a cold frame or greenhouse.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost risk passes to maintain a compact bushy shrub shape.
items.description: Tecticornia arbuscula, the shrubby glasswort or scrubby samphire, is a species of plant in the family Amaranthaceae, native to Australia. It is a shrub that grows to 2 metres in height, with a spreading habit. It has succulent swollen branchlets with small leaf lobes.

items.name: Bassia prostrata
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly at a depth of three millimetres in April using a free-draining gritty compost
Water sparingly only when the top two inches of soil are dry to prevent root rot in damp UK weather
Position in full sun and shelter from cold winds using a south-facing wall to mimic steppe heat
Grow in poor alkaline soil with added horticultural grit to prevent lush but weak floppy growth
Protect young spring shoots from slugs and snails using organic wool pellets or beer traps
items.description: Bassia prostrata, the forage kochia, is a Eurasian plant in the subfamily Camphorosmoideae of the family Amaranthaceae, introduced to the United States as rangeland forage and for fire control.

items.name: Sclerolaena bicornis
items.growersTips:
Grow in a free-draining gravel-rich loam with a neutral to alkaline pH to prevent winter root rot.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot or under a rain shelter to mimic dry Australian heat.
Water only during prolonged summer droughts and keep completely dry throughout the wet UK winter.
Prune back leggy stems in late spring after the last frost to maintain a compact, bushy habit.
Grow in terracotta pots that can be moved into a cold greenhouse or conservatory during winter.
items.description: Sclerolaena bicornis, commonly known as goathead burr, is a perennial shrub in the Amaranthaceae family, native to inland Australia, and found in Queensland, the Northern Territory, South Australia, New South Wales, and Western Australia The Walmajarri people of the Kimberley know the plant as Paka.

items.name: Salicornia virginica
items.growersTips:
Grow in a free-draining sandy loam mixed with horticultural grit to mimic coastal salt marshes.
Water weekly with a saline solution of one teaspoon of non-iodized sea salt per litre of rainwater.
Sow seeds in spring by pressing them lightly into damp compost without burying them as they need light.
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot to cope with cool damp UK summers and prevent rot.
Harvest the tender green tips in summer by pinching them out to encourage a bushier growth habit.
items.description: Salicornia virginica is a halophytic perennial dicot which grows in various zones of intertidal salt marshes and can be found in alkaline flats. It is native to various regions of the Northern Hemisphere including both coasts of North America from Canada to Mexico.

items.name: Maireana microcarpa
items.growersTips:
Grow in a terracotta pot with 50% grit to survive wet UK winters and move indoors before first frost
Water only when the compost is bone dry, mimicking its native Australian arid desert environment
Prune lightly in late spring after new growth starts to maintain a compact, bushy shrub shape
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot or unheated greenhouse to maximise essential summer heat
Avoid rich organic fertilisers which cause weak, floppy growth; use a very dilute cactus feed once
items.description: Maireana microcarpa, commonly known as swamp bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to south-eastern, continental Australia. It is a weakly upright shrub with slender branches covered with woolly white hairs when young, fleshy, terete leaves, flowers arranged singly and a dark brown or pale, tube-shaped fruiting perianth with a simple wing.

items.name: Halocnemum strobilaceum
items.growersTips:
Sow seeds shallowly in spring under glass using a free-draining sandy compost with added grit.
Water sparingly from below to keep the soil barely damp, avoiding any waterlogging at the roots.
Grow in pots of loam-based compost mixed with horticultural sand to mimic coastal salt marsh soils.
Place containers in the sunniest south-facing spot to maximise light and warmth in the UK climate.
Overwinter young plants in a cold frame or unheated greenhouse to protect them from excessive rain.
items.description: Halocnemum strobilaceum is a species of flowering plant in the subfamily Salicornioideae of the family Amaranthaceae. It is native to coastal areas of the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea and parts of the Middle East and central Asia, where it grows in coastal and inland salt marshes, alkali flats, and other habitats with saline soils.

items.name: Maireana coronata
items.growersTips:
Grow in free-draining gritty loam with added horticultural grit to survive wet UK winter wetness.
Keep in a terracotta pot to move indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or conservatory from November.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, reducing to zero during winter.
Prune back lightly in early spring after frosts pass to maintain a compact, bushy dome shape.
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot to maximise light levels during dull UK summers.
items.description: Maireana coronata, commonly known as crown fissure-weed, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a low-lying to erect perennial plant with linear leaves, bisexual flowers arranged singly, and a hairy fruiting perianth resembling an inverted academic "mortar board" hat, with a narrow circular wing.

items.name: Maireana murrayana
items.growersTips:
Grow in free-draining gritty loam with added horticultural grit to survive wet UK winters.
Plant in a terracotta pot to easily move indoors to a frost-free greenhouse before November frosts.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, reducing to zero during winter.
Prune lightly in late spring after the last frost to maintain a compact, bushy shrub shape.
Position in your garden's hottest, most south-facing suntrap to mimic its native arid habitat.
items.description: Maireana murrayana is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to inland Western Australia. It is shrub with its branchlets and leaves covered with woolly hairs, thick and fleshy, narrowly oblong to wedge-shaped leaves, bisexual, woolly, spherical flowers, and a glabrous fruiting perianth with a thin, horizontal wing.

items.name: Maireana microphylla
items.growersTips:
Grow in free-draining gritty soil or gravel beds to prevent winter root rot in wet UK climates.
Overwinter in a cold greenhouse or move container plants indoors before the first autumn frosts hit.
Water sparingly only when the top five centimetres of soil are bone dry, avoiding winter watering.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost risk passes to maintain a compact, bushy shrub shape.
Position in the sunniest, most south-facing sheltered spot in your garden to maximise summer heat.
items.description: Maireana microphylla, commonly known as cotton bush, small-leaf bluebush or eastern cottonbush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is a widely-branched shrub with slender branches, more or less terete leaves, flowers arranged singly but forming dense, leafy spikes and a tube-shaped fruiting perianth with a simple wing with a notched edge.

items.name: Maireana pentagona
items.growersTips:
Grow in a free-draining gritty loam with neutral to alkaline pH to prevent winter root rot in wet UK soils
Position in a terracotta pot in full sun so you can move it under glass to overwinter dry at 5C
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry during the active spring growing season
Sow seeds five millimetres deep in a heated propagator at twenty degrees Celsius during early spring
Prune back by one third in late spring to maintain a compact habit and prevent the stems going woody
items.description: Maireana pentagona, commonly known as hairy bluebush or slender fissure-weed, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, and is endemic to Australia. It is a prostrate to low-lying perennial with woolly branches, densely hairy linear leaves, flowers arranged singly and a woolly fruiting perianth, the upper surface with a thick, hard ridge.

items.name: Maireana decalvans
items.growersTips:
Grow in free-draining gritty soil with added perlite to prevent root rot during wet UK winters.
Position in a terracotta pot to move indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or conservatory by October.
Water only when the top five centimetres of compost is bone dry, reducing to once a month in winter.
Prune back leggy stems by one third in early spring to encourage a bushier, more compact habit.
Sow seeds five millimetres deep in spring using a heated propagator set to twenty-one degrees.
items.description: Maireana decalvans, commonly known as black cottonbush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a erect to spreading perennial plant with fleshy, terete to narrowly spindle-shaped leaves, glabrous, bisexual flowers arranged singly, and a hairy fruiting perianth with a hemispherical tube and a thin-walled wing.

items.name: Maireana pentatropis
items.growersTips:
Grow in free-draining gravelly soil with added grit to prevent winter root rot in wet UK climates.
Position in a terracotta pot to move indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or conservatory for winter.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, reducing to once a month in winter.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost passes to maintain a compact shape and remove dead wood.
Plant alongside rosemary or lavender which share its need for low-nutrient soil and full sun.
items.description: Maireana pentatropis commonly known as erect mallee bluebush,is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a small upright shrub with greyish woolly branches and fleshy leaves.

items.name: Maireana oppositifolia
items.growersTips:
Plant this Australian bluebush in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit to survive UK wet winters.
Move the container under a cold glasshouse or south-facing porch from November to March to dry out.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, reducing to once a month in winter.
Prune the stems by one third in late spring after frosts pass to maintain a compact shrubby habit.
Position in your garden's hottest microclimate against a south-facing brick wall for maximum sun.
items.description: Maireana oppositifolia, commonly known as heathy bluebush is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to the south of continental Australia. It is compact, usually dioecious shrub with woolly branches when young, narrowly egg-shaped leaves usually arranged in opposite pairs, flowers arranged singly, and a glabrous, thin-walled fruiting perianth with a fan-shaped, prominently-veined wing.

items.name: Maireana ovata
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Australian shrub in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit to survive UK wet.
Bring containers indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or conservatory from October through to April.
Water only when the compost is bone dry, reducing to once a month during the cold winter dormancy.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost risk passes to maintain its compact rounded shrub shape.
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot to mimic its native arid habitat and prevent root rot.
items.description: Maireana ovata is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to central Australia. It is a small, densely branched shrub with densely woolly branches, narrowly egg-shaped to broadly triangular leaves, bisexual flowers and a fruiting perianth with a translucent wing.

items.name: Tecticornia halocnemoides
items.growersTips:
Grow in a free-draining 50% grit and sand mix to mimic saline flats and prevent winter root rot.
Keep in a container to move indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or conservatory from November to March.
Water sparingly only when the top five centimetres of soil dry out, reducing to zero during winter.
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot or under grow lights to compensate for low UK light.
Prune lightly in late spring by pinching out stem tips to encourage a bushier shrubby habit.
items.description: Tecticornia halocnemoides, commonly known as shrubby samphire or grey glasswort, is a species of succulent, salt tolerant plant endemic to Australia. It grows as a spreading or erect shrub up to fifty centimetres high. It was first published as Arthrocnemum halocnemoides in 1845, but transferred into Halosarcia in 1980, and into Tecticornia in 2007.

items.name: Maireana villosa
items.growersTips:
Grow this Australian shrub in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit to survive wet UK winters.
Move the pot into an unheated greenhouse or porch from November to March to prevent root rot.
Water only when the compost is completely dry, using a soak and dry method during summer months.
Prune lightly in late spring after the last frost to maintain a compact shape and encourage growth.
Position in the absolute brightest spot of your garden, facing south to maximise scarce UK sunlight.
items.description: Maireana villosa, commonly known as silky bluebush, or common bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to mainland Australia. It is an open, hairy, ascending subshrub or shrub with semi-succulent linear to oblong or narrowly lance-shaped leaves with the narrower end towards the base, mostly bisexual flowers arranged singly or in pairs, and a fruiting perianth with a more or less horizontal wing with a radial slit.

items.name: Maireana polypterygia
items.growersTips:
Grow in free-draining gravelly soil with added grit to survive wet UK winters and prevent root rot.
Position in a terracotta pot to easily move indoors to a frost-free greenhouse during winter cold.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil are bone dry, mimicking its arid native habitat.
Prune lightly in late spring after the last frost to maintain a compact shape and remove dead wood.
Plant alongside Mediterranean herbs like rosemary and thyme which share its low-moisture requirements.
items.description: Maireana polypterygia, commonly known as many-winged bluebush or Gascoyne bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, and is endemic to the north-west of Western Australia. It is a rounded, usually dioecious shrub with woolly branchlets, almost terete to spoon-shaped leaves, glabrous flowers arranged singly, and a glabrous fruiting perianth with several papery, imperfectly developed horizontal wings.

items.name: Maireana dichoptera
items.growersTips:
Grow in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit to survive wet UK winters and prevent root rot.
Bring containers indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or conservatory from October through to April.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, reducing to once a month in winter.
Prune back leggy stems by one third in late spring to encourage a bushier, more compact habit.
Position in your garden's hottest, most south-facing spot to maximise essential summer sunlight.
items.description: Maireana dichoptera is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to northern Australia. It is an erect perennial plant with woolly branches, linear leaves with shaggy hairs pressed against the surface, bisexual flowers arranged singly or in pairs, and a thin-walled fruiting perianth with a six vertical wings on top of a horizontal wing.

items.name: Maireana prosthecochaeta
items.growersTips:
Grow this Australian native in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit to survive wet UK winters.
Water only when the compost is bone dry during summer and keep completely dry from October to March.
Place the pot in your garden's hottest south-facing sun trap or keep it in an unheated greenhouse.
Prune lightly in late spring after the last frost to maintain its compact shrubby shape.
Group with potted Mediterranean herbs like rosemary to share similar dry soil and sun requirements.
items.description: Maireana prosthecochaeta is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, and is endemic to the north-west of Western Australia. It is an open, densely-leaved, glabrous shrub with erect branches, almost terete leaves, bisexual flowers arranged singly, and a glabrous, dark brown fruiting perianth with a horizontal wing.

items.name: Maireana amoena
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Australian shrub in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit to survive UK wet.
Bring the pot indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or bright windowsill from October to April.
Water only when the compost is bone dry, reducing to once a month during the damp winter months.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost risk passes to maintain a compact, bushy shrub shape.
Position in your garden's hottest, most south-facing sun trap to mimic its native desert heat.
items.description: Maireana amoena is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Western Australia. It is a small, brittle shrub with fleshy, spherical, oval or terete leaves, pairs of male and female flowers, and a hemispherical utricle with a short tube and horizontal wings.

items.name: Maireana astrotricha
items.growersTips:
Grow in a free-draining gritty loam with a pH of 7 to 8 to prevent root rot in wet UK winters.
Overwinter in a heated greenhouse or conservatory as this plant cannot survive UK frosts below -5C.
Water only when the soil is completely dry, reducing to once a month from November through March.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost risk passes to maintain a compact, bushy silver mound.
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot or against a warm wall to maximise summer heat.
items.description: Maireana astrotricha, commonly known as low bluebush, southern bluebush, or grey bluebush, is a widely branched, perennial plant with fleshy leaves, male, female or bisexual flowers and a winged fruiting perianth, and is usually found growing in open habitats, typically in gravelly, well-drained soils, in New South Wales, Queensland and the Northern Territory.

items.name: Maireana scleroptera
items.growersTips:
Grow in free-draining gritty loam with added horticultural sand to prevent winter root rot in UK rain
Keep in a terracotta pot to overwinter indoors or in a heated greenhouse before first autumn frosts
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, reducing to once a month in winter
Prune back leggy stems by one third in late spring to encourage a bushier habit and fresh foliage
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot or gravel garden to maximise crucial summer warmth
items.description: Maireana scleroptera, commonly known as hard-wing bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to arid parts of inland Australia. It is a prostrate to erect perennial with narrowly oblong to narrowly egg-shaped leaves, pairs of densely woolly bisexual flowers, and a cartilaginous to woody hemispherical fruiting perianth with five broadly oblong, horizontal wings.

items.name: Maireana spongiocarpa
items.growersTips:
Grow this Australian shrub in a terracotta pot with 50% grit to survive wet UK winters outdoors.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, as this species easily rots.
Place the pot against a south-facing brick wall to maximise heat and shield it from cold winds.
Bring the plant into an unheated greenhouse or conservatory from November to March to avoid frost.
Prune lightly in late spring by pinching out stem tips to encourage a bushier, compact habit.
items.description: Maireana spongiocarpa, commonly known as spongy-fruit bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Central Australia. It is a small shrub with thin woolly branches, well-spaced fleshy, narrowly terete or spindle-shaped leaves, bisexual flowers and a soft, easily crushed fruiting perianth with a broadly top-shaped, spongy, swollen tube with a horizontal wing.

items.name: Maireana cannonii
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Australian shrub in a gritty, free-draining loam with a pH between 6.5 and 7.5.
Keep in a pot and move indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or conservatory from October to April.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, reducing to once a month in winter.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost risk passes to maintain a compact, bushy foliage shape.
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot to mimic its native arid light levels and heat.
items.description: Maireana cannonii, commonly known as Cannon's bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to South Australia. It is a small subshrub with many branches, sessile leaves arranged in opposite pairs, bisexual flowers arranged singly, and a crust-like, hemispherical fruiting perianth with a thin, horizontal wing.

items.name: Tecticornia indica
items.growersTips:
Grow this salt-tolerant halophyte in a free-draining gritty sand mix with added horticultural salt.
Overwinter container-grown plants in a heated greenhouse or conservatory to survive UK frosts.
Water sparingly from below only when the top five centimetres of sandy substrate are bone dry.
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot or under grow lights to mimic its arid native habitat.
Prune back dead woody stems in late spring once new succulent green shoots begin to emerge.
items.description: Tecticornia indica is a species of plant that is succulent and halophyte which grows in salt marshes on tropical areas of the world. This plant belongs to the Chenopodiaceae, which are now included in family Amaranthaceae.

items.name: Maireana thesioides
items.growersTips:
Grow in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit to survive wet winters and prevent root rot.
Bring the pot indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or conservatory from November through to March.
Water only when the compost is bone dry, reducing to once a month during the damp winter months.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost risk passes to maintain a compact, bushy shrub shape.
Position in the absolute sunniest, south-facing spot in your garden to mimic arid conditions.
items.description: Maireana thesioides, commonly known as mulga bluebush or lax bluebush, is a plant in the Amaranthaceae family and is endemic to Western Australia. It is a weak, straggly, mostly glabrous shrub with slender, often drooping branches, fleshy, narrowly spindle-shaped leaves, flowers arranged singly and a crusty, glabrous fruiting perianth with a thin, horizontal wing.

items.name: Maireana trichoptera
items.growersTips:
Grow in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit to survive wet UK winters and prevent root rot.
Bring the pot indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or bright windowsill from November to March.
Water only when the compost is bone dry, reducing to once a month during the cold winter dormancy.
Position in the sunniest south-facing spot in your garden to mimic its native Australian heat.
Prune back by one third in early spring to encourage bushy new growth and prevent leggy stems.
items.description: Maireana trichoptera, commonly known as mallee bluebush, pink-seeded bluebush or downy bluebush, or spike bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, native to all mainland states and territories of Australia except Queensland. It is an erect perennial shrub with white, woolly branches, fleshy semiterete leaves, white bisexual flowers arranged singly, and a hairy fruiting perianth with a thin, horizontal wing.

items.name: Maireana triptera
items.growersTips:
Grow this Australian native in a terracotta pot using a fifty-fifty mix of grit and loam-based compost.
Bring the pot indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or conservatory from late October until mid-May.
Water only when the soil is bone dry, reducing to once a month during the damp UK winter months.
Prune lightly by pinching out stem tips in late spring to encourage a bushy, compact growth habit.
Position the pot in your garden's hottest, most south-facing sun trap to maximise summer heat.
items.description: Maireana triptera, commonly known as three-wing bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to mainland Australia. It is a glaucous, compact perennial shrub with mostly glabrous branchlets, fleshy semiterete leaves, mostly bisexual flowers arranged singly, and a glabrous fruiting perianth with five vertical wings fused to a horizontal wing.

items.name: Maireana atkinsiana
items.growersTips:
Grow in free-draining gritty loam with added horticultural sand to prevent winter root rot in UK rain.
Position in a terracotta pot to easily move indoors to a frost-free greenhouse during wet winters.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, reducing to zero during winter dormancy.
Prune lightly in late spring after frosts pass to shape the shrub and encourage fresh silver foliage.
Plant alongside rosemary or lavender which share its strict requirement for dry, alkaline soil.
items.description: Maireana atkinsiana, commonly known as bronze bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Western Australia. It is a rigid, brittle, dioecious shrub with fleshy, narrowly to broadly egg-shaped leaves with the narrower end towards the base, pairs of male and female flowers, and a pink to red, thin-walled fruiting perianth.

items.name: Maireana cheelii
items.growersTips:
Grow in free-draining gritty loam with a neutral to alkaline pH to prevent root rot in wet winters.
Position in a terracotta pot to easily move indoors to a frost-free greenhouse during UK frosts.
Water sparingly only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, keeping dry in winter.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost risk passes to maintain a compact, bushy growth habit.
Plant alongside hardy sedums or sempervivums which share its need for dry, sun-baked conditions.
items.description: Maireana cheelii, commonly known as chariot wheels, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is a small, erect perennial with more or less terete leaves, bisexual flowers arranged singly or in pairs, and a stiff, cottony fruiting perianth with a wheel-shaped wing.

items.name: Sclerolaena anisacanthoides
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Australian subshrub in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit for sharp drainage.
Overwinter containers indoors under glass to protect this arid-loving plant from wet UK winter rot.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, keeping it completely dry in winter.
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot or unheated greenhouse to mimic its native heat levels.
Prune back leggy stems by one third in late spring to maintain a compact shape and encourage growth.
items.description: Sclerolaena anisacanthoides, the yellow burr, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, native to eastern Australia. A perennial rounded subshrub reaching 15 cm (6 in), it is typically found growing in heavy soils.

items.name: Sclerolaena birchii
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Australian native in a terracotta pot with fifty percent grit to survive UK wet.
Keep soil completely dry during winter by moving the container into a frost-free greenhouse or shed.
Water only when the potting mix is bone dry, applying a light soak at the base to prevent stem rot.
Wear thick leather gloves when handling to protect your hands from the extremely sharp woody spines.
Position in your garden's hottest, most sun-baked spot to mimic its arid natural desert habitat.
items.description: Sclerolaena birchii, commonly known as galvanised burr, is a perennial shrub native to inland Australia.

items.name: Sclerolaena densiflora
items.growersTips:
Grow in a gritty loam-based compost with fifty percent horticultural grit to prevent winter rot.
Overwinter this Australian native in a frost-free greenhouse or conservatory to survive UK damp.
Water only when the soil is completely dry during summer and keep entirely dry throughout winter.
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot or under glass to maximise essential heat and light.
Propagate by sowing seeds in spring using a heated propagator set to twenty-one degrees Celsius.
items.description: Sclerolaena densiflora is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, native to Western Australia. It was first described in 1904 by William Vincent Fitzgerald as Bassia densiflora, but was transferred to the genus, Sclerolaena in 1978 by Andrew John Scott.

items.name: Sclerolaena diacantha
items.growersTips:
Grow in a terracotta pot using a fifty-fifty mix of loam-based compost and coarse horticultural grit
Water only when the soil is completely dry from May to September and keep bone dry during winter
Overwinter indoors on a south-facing windowsill or in a heated greenhouse to prevent frost damage
Prune back leggy stems by one third in late spring to encourage a bushier habit and fresh growth
Position in the sunniest spot of the garden to maximize light levels and prevent rot from damp air
items.description: Sclerolaena diacantha, the grey copperburr, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, native to Australia. It is a perennial rounded subshrub reaching 30 cm (12 in), with a widespread distribution.

items.name: Sclerolaena calcarata
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Australian burr in a container of gritty, free-draining loam to move it indoors.
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot or unheated greenhouse to mimic its arid native habitat.
Water sparingly only when the soil is bone dry, keeping it completely dry during damp UK winters.
Wear thick leather gloves when handling to protect your hands from the sharp, spiny fruiting burrs.
Overwinter indoors on a sunny windowsill at temperatures kept strictly above five degrees Celsius.
items.description: Sclerolaena calcarata, the redburr, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, native to central and eastern Australia. A perennial rounded subshrub reaching 25 cm (10 in), it is typically found growing in heavy soils.

items.name: Sclerolaena eriacantha
items.growersTips:
Grow in a free-draining gravel-sand mix under glass to protect from persistent UK winter wet.
Water only when the soil is completely dry, reducing to zero moisture from November to March.
Position in a south-facing cold frame or unheated greenhouse to maximise scarce UK summer sun.
Propagate by sowing seeds in spring at a depth of three millimetres using a heated propagator.
Keep a close watch for glasshouse mealybugs on the woolly stems during humid summer months.
items.description: Sclerolaena eriacantha, commonly known as tall bindii, is a perennial shrub native to inland Australia.

items.name: Sclerolaena eurotioides
items.growersTips:
Grow in a free-draining gravel-rich loam with a pH of 7.0 to 8.5 to prevent winter root rot in UK wet.
Keep in a terracotta pot and move under a cold glass frame from October to March to avoid damp soil.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, reducing to zero during winter months.
Prune back leggy stems by one third in late April to maintain a compact shape and encourage growth.
Position in your sunniest south-facing spot to mimic the intense light of its native habitat.
items.description: Sclerolaena eurotioides is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, native to Western Australia. It was first described in 1869 by Ferdinand von Mueller as Echinopsilon eurotioides, but was transferred to the genus, Sclerolaena in 1978 by Andrew John Scott.

items.name: Maireana pyramidata
items.growersTips:
Grow in free-draining gritty soil with added perlite to prevent root rot during wet UK winters.
Position in a terracotta pot to move indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or conservatory by October.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, reducing to once a month in winter.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost passes to maintain a compact shape and remove dead wood.
Keep away from thirsty garden plants and pair with drought-tolerant sedums in a sunny gravel bed.
items.description: Maireana pyramidata is a species of flowering plant in family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Australia, where it is found in all mainland states and the Northern Territory. It is a compact, dense, stiffly branched shrub with hairy, spreading leaves, mostly unisexual flowers and a pale brown to black fruiting perianth with a papery wing.

items.name: Sclerolaena cornishiana
items.growersTips:
Grow this Australian native in a terracotta pot with 50 percent grit to survive wet UK winters.
Water only when the soil is bone dry, mimicking arid outback conditions to prevent root rot.
Position the pot in your hottest south-facing spot or an unheated greenhouse for maximum sun.
Prune back leggy stems by one third in late spring to maintain a compact and tidy growth habit.
Protect the plant indoors from November to March as it cannot tolerate frost and heavy UK rain.
items.description: Sclerolaena cornishiana, the cartwheel burr, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, native to parts of northern Australia. An annual or perennial, it is an intricately branched herb with solitary flowers.

items.name: Sclerolaena fimbriolata
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Australian shrub in a gritty, free-draining loam mix with fifty percent perlite.
Keep the plant in a pot to move indoors to a heated greenhouse before the first autumn frost.
Water only when the soil is completely dry, reducing to once a month during damp UK winters.
Place in your garden's hottest, most south-facing spot to mimic its native arid light levels.
Prune lightly in late spring after frost risk passes to maintain a compact, bushy shrub shape.
items.description: Sclerolaena fimbriolata is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, native to central Western Australia. A small shrub, it is typically found growing on the edges of gypsum salt lakes.

items.name: Maireana appressa
items.growersTips:
Grow this Australian native in a pot with fifty percent grit to survive wet UK winters outdoors.
Water only when the soil is completely dry, reducing to once a month from November to March.
Place the pot against a south-facing brick wall to maximise heat and shield from frost.
Prune lightly in late spring after the last frost to maintain a compact, bushy shape.
Avoid any high-nitrogen fertilisers as they cause weak, floppy growth on this desert shrub.
items.description: Maireana appressa, commonly known as grey bluebush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is an intricately branched, spreading or erect shrub covered with woolly, white hairs with narrowly triangular to narrowly oblong leaves, bisexual flowers arranged singly, and a top-shaped fruiting perianth with horizontal wings.

items.name: Maireana enchylaenoides
items.growersTips:
Grow this Australian native in a terracotta pot using a gritty, free-draining loam-based compost.
Bring the pot indoors to a frost-free greenhouse or bright windowsill from November to March.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, reducing to monthly in winter.
Prune back by one third in April to stimulate fresh, dense blue-green foliage and prevent legginess.
Position in your garden's hottest, most sun-baked spot, ideally against a south-facing brick wall.
items.description: Maireana enchylaenoides, commonly known as wingless bluebush or wingless fissure-weed, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a perennial herb with scattered, slightly fleshy, narrowly oblong leaves, bisexual flowers arranged singly, and a fruiting perianth with a thin-walled tube with 5 leathery wings.

items.name: Sclerolaena lanicuspis
items.growersTips:
Grow in a gritty loam-based compost with fifty percent horticultural grit to prevent winter rot.
Keep in unheated glasshouse staging over winter to protect from cold UK rain and frost damage.
Water only when the soil is bone dry from April to September and keep completely dry in winter.
Position in the brightest south-facing spot possible to mimic its arid Australian desert habitat.
Repot in spring using a shallow terracotta pan to accommodate its fibrous root system.
items.description: Sclerolaena lanicuspis, the spinach-burr or copper-burr, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae, native to Australia. A woody perennial reaching 25 cm (10 in), it has tomentose branches and semiterete leaves.

items.name: Sclerolaena tetracuspis
items.growersTips:
Grow this tender Australian shrub in a terracotta pot with 50% grit to survive wet UK winters.
Water only when the top five centimetres of soil is bone dry, keeping it completely dry in winter.
Position the pot in your hottest, south-facing sun trap or a cold greenhouse to mimic its desert home.
Prune lightly in late spring by pinching out growing tips to prevent the plant from becoming leggy.
Check the sharp, spiny burrs regularly for mealybugs which hide deep inside the leaf junctions.

items.name: Sclerolaena hostilis
items.growersTips:
Grow this Australian arid shrub in a terracotta pot using a fifty-fifty mix of grit and loam.
Keep the plant completely dry during wet UK winters by moving the pot into a cold greenhouse.
Position in your garden's hottest south-facing spot to mimic its native desert heat and light.
Water only when the soil is bone dry, applying a deep soak once a fortnight in midsummer.
Wear thick leather gloves when handling to avoid the extremely sharp spines on the seed burrs.

items.name: Sclerolaena tricuspis
items.growersTips:
Grow this Australian native in a terracotta pot using a fifty-fifty mix of grit and John Innes No 1.
Water only when the compost is bone dry, reducing to zero watering from November through to March.
Keep the plant in a heated greenhouse or bright conservatory over winter to protect from UK frosts.
Prune back leggy stems by one third in late spring using thick gloves to avoid the sharp spines.
Position in your garden's hottest south-facing spot to maximise the limited UK summer sunshine.

items.name: Maireana eriantha
items.growersTips:
